  445 | # Terminology
  446 | Trakt has a lot of features and here's a chart to help explain the differences between some of them.
  447 | 
  448 | | Term | Description |
  449 | |---|---|
  450 | | `scrobble` | Automatic way to track what a user is watching in a media center. |
  451 | | `checkin` | Manual action used by mobile apps allowing the user to indicate what they are watching right now. |
  452 | | `history` | All watched items (scrobbles, checkins, watched) for a user. |
  453 | | `collection` | Items a user has available to watch including Blu-Rays, DVDs, and digital downloads. |
  454 | | `watchlist` | Items a user wants to watch in the future. Once watched, they are auto removed from this list. |
  455 | | `list` | Personal list for any purpose. Items are not auto removed from any personal lists. |
  456 | | `favorites` | A user's top 50 TV shows and movies. |
  457 | 
  458 | # Group Authentication - OAuth
  459 | The API uses OAuth2.  If you know what's up with OAuth2, grab your library and starting rolling. If you have access to a web browser (mobile app, desktop app, website), use standard **OAuth**. If you don't have web browser access (media center plugins, smart watches, smart TVs, command line scripts, system services), use **Device** authentication.
  460 | 
  461 | To obtain a `client_id` and `client_secret`, create an application on the Trakt website. Here are some helpful links to get your started:
  462 | 
  463 | - [Create a new API app](https://trakt.tv/oauth/applications/new)
  464 | - [View your API apps](https://trakt.tv/oauth/applications)
  465 | 
  466 | ---
  467 | 
  468 | #### Application Flow
  469 | 
  470 | 1. **Redirect to request Trakt access.** Using the [**/oauth/authorize**](/reference/authentication-oauth/authorize) method, construct then redirect to this URL. The Trakt website will request permissions for your app and the user will have the opportunity to sign up for a new Trakt account or sign in with their existing account.
  471 | 2. **Trakt redirects back to your site.** If the user accepts your request, Trakt redirects back to your site with a temporary code in a `code` GET parameter as well as the state (if provided) in the previous step in a `state` parameter. If the states don’t match, the request has been created by a third party and the process should be aborted.
  472 | 3. **Exchange the code for an access token.** If everything looks good in step 2, exchange the `code` for an access token using the [**/oauth/token**](reference/authentication-oauth/get-token/) method. Save the `access_token` so your app can authenticate the user by sending the `Authorization` header as indicated below or in any example code. The `access_token` is valid for **24 hours**. Save and use the `refresh_token` to get a new `access_token` without asking the user to re-authenticate.
  473 | 
  474 | ## Authorize [/oauth/authorize{?response_type,client_id,redirect_uri,state}]
  475 | 
  476 | + Parameters
  477 |     + response_type (required, string, `code`) ... Must be set to code.
  478 |     + client_id (required, string, ` `) ... Get this from your app settings.
  479 |     + redirect_uri (required, string, ` `) ... URI specified in your app settings.
  480 |     + state (optional, string, ` `) ... State variable for CSRF purposes.
  481 |     + signup (optional, string, `true`) ... Default to the sign up page.
  482 | 
  483 | ### Authorize Application [GET]
  484 | Construct then redirect to this URL. The Trakt website will request permissions for your app, which the user needs to approve. If the user isn't signed into Trakt, it will ask them to do so.
  485 | 
  486 | > ### ☣️ 🅸🅼🅿🅾🆁🆃🅰🅽🆃
  487 | > _Use the website **https://trakt.tv** hostname when creating this URL and not the API URL._
  488 | 
  489 | #### Optional URL Parameters
  490 | 
  491 | When building the authorization URL, you can optionally include the following query parameters in the URL.
  492 | 
  493 | | Parameter | Value | Description |
  494 | |---|---|---|
  495 | | `signup` | `true` | Prefer the account sign up page to be the default. |
  496 | | `prompt` | `login` | Force the user to sign in and authorize your app. |
  497 | 
  498 | + Request (application/json)
  499 | 
  500 |     ```
  501 |     https://trakt.tv/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=9b36d8c0db59eff5038aea7a417d73e69aea75b41aac771816d2ef1b3109cc2f&redirect_uri=urn:ietf:wg:oauth:2.0:oob
  502 |     ```
  503 | 
  504 |     + Body
  505 | 
  506 | + Response 200
  507 | 
  508 |     + Body
  509 | 
  510 | ## Get Token [/oauth/token]
  511 | 
  512 | ### Exchange code for access_token [POST]
  513 | Use the authorization `code` GET parameter sent back to your `redirect_uri` to get an `access_token`. Save the `access_token` so your app can authenticate the user by sending the `Authorization` header.
  514 | 
  515 | The `access_token` is valid for **24 hours**. Save and use the `refresh_token` to get a new `access_token` without asking the user to re-authenticate.
  516 | 
  517 | #### JSON POST Data
  518 | | Key | Type | Value |
  519 | |---|---|---|
  520 | | `code` <span style="color:red;">*</a> | string | Authorization code. |
  521 | | `client_id` <span style="color:red;">*</a> | string | Get this from your app settings. |
  522 | | `client_secret` <span style="color:red;">*</a> | string | Get this from your app settings. |
  523 | | `redirect_uri` <span style="color:red;">*</a> | string | URI specified in your app settings. |
  524 | | `grant_type` <span style="color:red;">* </a> | string | `authorization_code` |
  525 | 
  526 | + Request (application/json)
  527 | 
  528 |     + Body
  529 | 
  530 |             {
  531 |                 "code": "fd0847dbb559752d932dd3c1ac34ff98d27b11fe2fea5a864f44740cd7919ad0",
  532 |                 "client_id": "9b36d8c0db59eff5038aea7a417d73e69aea75b41aac771816d2ef1b3109cc2f",
  533 |                 "client_secret": "d6ea27703957b69939b8104ed4524595e210cd2e79af587744a7eb6e58f5b3d2",
  534 |                 "redirect_uri": "urn:ietf:wg:oauth:2.0:oob",
  535 |                 "grant_type": "authorization_code"
  536 |             }
  537 | 
  538 | + Response 200 (application/json)
  539 | 
  540 |     If the `code` is valid, you'll get the `access_token` back.
  541 | 
  542 |     + Body
  543 | 
  544 |             {
  545 |                 "access_token": "dbaf9757982a9e738f05d249b7b5b4a266b3a139049317c4909f2f263572c781",
  546 |                 "token_type": "bearer",
  547 |                 "expires_in": 86400,
  548 |                 "refresh_token": "76ba4c5c75c96f6087f58a4de10be6c00b29ea1ddc3b2022ee2016d1363e3a7c",
  549 |                 "scope": "public",
  550 |                 "created_at": 1487889741
  551 |             }
  552 | 
  553 | + Response 401 (application/json)
  554 | 
  555 |     If the `code` is invalid, you'll get a `401` error.
  556 | 
  557 |     + Body
  558 | 
  559 |             {
  560 |                 "error": "invalid_grant",
  561 |                 "error_description": "The provided authorization grant is invalid, expired, revoked, does not match the redirection URI used in the authorization request, or was issued to another client."
  562 |             }
  563 | 
  564 | ## Refresh Token [/oauth/token]
  565 | 
  566 | ### Exchange refresh_token for access_token [POST]
  567 | Use the `refresh_token` to get a new `access_token` without asking the user to re-authenticate. The `access_token` is valid for **24 hours** before it needs to be refreshed again.
  568 | 
  569 | #### JSON POST Data
  570 | | Key | Type | Value |
  571 | |---|---|---|
  572 | | `refresh_token` <span style="color:red;">*</a> | string | Saved from the initial token method. |
  573 | | `client_id` <span style="color:red;">*</a> | string | Get this from your app settings. |
  574 | | `client_secret` <span style="color:red;">*</a> | string | Get this from your app settings. |
  575 | | `redirect_uri` <span style="color:red;">*</a> | string | URI specified in your app settings. |
  576 | | `grant_type` <span style="color:red;">* </a> | string | `refresh_token` |
  577 | 
  578 | + Request (application/json)
  579 | 
  580 |     + Body
  581 | 
  582 |             {
  583 |                 "refresh_token": "fd0847dbb559752d932dd3c1ac34ff98d27b11fe2fea5a864f44740cd7919ad0",
  584 |                 "client_id": "9b36d8c0db59eff5038aea7a417d73e69aea75b41aac771816d2ef1b3109cc2f",
  585 |                 "client_secret": "d6ea27703957b69939b8104ed4524595e210cd2e79af587744a7eb6e58f5b3d2",
  586 |                 "redirect_uri": "urn:ietf:wg:oauth:2.0:oob",
  587 |                 "grant_type": "refresh_token"
  588 |             }
  589 | 
  590 | + Response 200 (application/json)
  591 | 
  592 |     If the `refresh_token` is valid, you'll get the `access_token` back.
  593 | 
  594 |     + Body
  595 | 
  596 |             {
  597 |                 "access_token": "dbaf9757982a9e738f05d249b7b5b4a266b3a139049317c4909f2f263572c781",
  598 |                 "token_type": "bearer",
  599 |                 "expires_in": 86400,
  600 |                 "refresh_token": "76ba4c5c75c96f6087f58a4de10be6c00b29ea1ddc3b2022ee2016d1363e3a7c",
  601 |                 "scope": "public",
  602 |                 "created_at": 1487889741
  603 |             }
  604 | 
  605 | + Response 401 (application/json)
  606 | 
  607 |     If the `refresh_token` is invalid, you'll get a `401` error.
  608 | 
  609 |     + Body
  610 | 
  611 |             {
  612 |                 "error": "invalid_grant",
  613 |                 "error_description": "The provided authorization grant is invalid, expired, revoked, does not match the redirection URI used in the authorization request, or was issued to another client."
  614 |             }
  615 | 
  616 | ## Revoke Token [/oauth/revoke]
  617 | 
  618 | ### Revoke an access_token [POST]
  619 | An `access_token` can be revoked when a user signs out of their Trakt account in your app. This is not required, but might improve the user experience so the user doesn't have an unused app connection hanging around.
  620 | 
  621 | #### JSON POST Data
  622 | | Key | Type | Value |
  623 | |---|---|---|
  624 | | `token` <span style="color:red;">*</a> | string | A valid OAuth `access_token`. |
  625 | | `client_id` <span style="color:red;">*</a> | string | Get this from your app settings. |
  626 | | `client_secret` <span style="color:red;">*</a> | string | Get this from your app settings. |
  627 |

  643 | 
  644 | # Group Authentication - Devices
  645 | Device authentication is for apps and services with limited input or display capabilities. This include media center plugins, smart watches, smart TVs, command line scripts, and system services.
  646 | 
  647 | Your app displays an alphanumeric code (typically 8 characters) to the user. They are then instructed to visit the verification URL on their computer or mobile device. After entering the code, the user will be prompted to grant permission for your app. After your app gets permissions, the device receives an `access_token` and works like standard OAuth from that point on. More details below.
  648 | 
  649 | ---
  650 | 
  651 | #### Application Flow
  652 | 
  653 | 1. **Generate codes.** Your app calls [**/oauth/device/code**](/reference/authentication-devices/code) to generate new codes. Save this entire response for later use.
  654 | 2. **Display the code.** Display the `user_code` and instruct the user to visit the `verification_url` on their computer or mobile device.
  655 | 3. **Poll for authorization.** Poll the [**/oauth/device/token**](/reference/authentication-devices/token) method to see if the user successfully authorizes your app. Use the `device_code` and poll at the `interval` (in seconds) to check if the user has authorized your app. Check the docs below for the specific error codes you need to handle. Use `expires_in` to stop polling after that many seconds, and gracefully instruct the user to restart the process. **It is important to poll at the correct interval and also stop polling when expired.**
  656 | 4. **Successful authorization.** When you receive a `200` success response, save the `access_token` so your app can authenticate the user in methods that require it. The `access_token` is valid for **24 hours**. Save and use the `refresh_token` to get a new `access_token` without asking the user to re-authenticate. It's normal OAuth from this point.
  657 | 
  658 | ---
  659 | 
  660 | #### User Flow
  661 | 
  662 | 1. **Call to action.** Consider your user experience when asking a user to connect their Trakt account. For some devices this will be right away, and for others it might be later in the experience.
  663 | 2. **Display the code.** When a user clicks the call to action, your app calls [**/oauth/device/code**](/reference/authentication-devices/code) to generate new codes. In your UI, display the `user_code` and instruct the user to visit the `verification_url` on their computer or mobile device. The `user_code` is typically 8 characters, so make sure there is enough room to display the full code.
  664 | 3. **Authorizing your app.** When the user visits the `verification_url` it first checks to make sure they're signed in. If not signed in, they'll be able to or can sign up for a new account. After entering the code, the user will be prompted to grant permission for your app. Once approved, the user will see a success message indicating their device is connected.
  665 | 4. **Confirm successful authorization.** Your app will be polling to see if the user successfully authorizes your app. Once they have, refresh your UI to indicate a successful connection has been made.
  666 | 
  667 | ## Device Code [/oauth/device/code]
  668 | 
  669 | ### Generate new device codes [POST]
  670 | Generate new codes to start the device authentication process. The `device_code` and `interval` will be used later to poll for the `access_token`. The `user_code` and `verification_url` should be presented to the user as mentioned in the flow steps above.
  671 | 
  672 | #### QR Code
  673 | 
  674 | You might consider generating a QR code for the user to easily scan on their mobile device. The QR code should be a URL that redirects to the `verification_url` and appends the `user_code`. For example, `https://trakt.tv/activate/5055CC52` would load the Trakt hosted `verification_url` and pre-fill in the `user_code`.
  675 | 
  676 | #### JSON POST Data
  677 | | Key | Type | Value |
  678 | |---|---|---|
  679 | | `client_id` <span style="color:red;">*</a> | string | Get this from your app settings. |
  680 | 
  681 | + Request (application/json)
  682 | 
  683 |     + Body
  684 | 
  685 |             {
  686 |                 "client_id": "9b36d8c0db59eff5038aea7a417d73e69aea75b41aac771816d2ef1b3109cc2f"
  687 |             }
  688 | 
  689 | + Response 200 (application/json)
  690 | 
  691 |     + Body
  692 | 
  693 |             {
  694 |                 "device_code": "d9c126a7706328d808914cfd1e40274b6e009f684b1aca271b9b3f90b3630d64",
  695 |                 "user_code": "5055CC52",
  696 |                 "verification_url": "https://trakt.tv/activate",
  697 |                 "expires_in": 600,
  698 |                 "interval": 5
  699 |             }
  700 | 
  701 | ## Get Token [/oauth/device/token]
  702 | 
  703 | ### Poll for the access_token [POST]
  704 | Use the `device_code` and poll at the `interval` (in seconds) to check if the user has authorized you app. Use `expires_in` to stop polling after that many seconds, and gracefully instruct the user to restart the process. **It is important to poll at the correct interval and also stop polling when expired.**
  705 | 
  706 | When you receive a `200` success response, save the `access_token` so your app can authenticate the user in methods that require it. The `access_token` is valid for **24 hours**. Save and use the `refresh_token` to get a new `access_token` without asking the user to re-authenticate. Check below for all the error codes that you should handle.
  707 | 
  708 | #### JSON POST Data
  709 | | Key | Type | Value |
  710 | |---|---|---|
  711 | | `code` <span style="color:red;">*</a> | string | `device_code` from the initial method. |
  712 | | `client_id` <span style="color:red;">*</a> | string | Get this from your app settings. |
  713 | | `client_secret` <span style="color:red;">*</a> | string | Get this from your app settings. |
  714 | 
  715 | #### Status Codes
  716 | This method will send various HTTP status codes that you should handle accordingly.
  717 | 
  718 | | Code | Description |
  719 | |---|---|
  720 | | `200` | Success - *save the `access_token`*
  721 | | `400` | Pending - *waiting for the user to authorize your app*
  722 | | `404` | Not Found - *invalid `device_code`*
  723 | | `409` | Already Used - *user already approved this code*
  724 | | `410` | Expired - *the tokens have expired, restart the process*
  725 | | `418` | Denied - *user explicitly denied this code*
  726 | | `429` | Slow Down - *your app is polling too quickly*
  727 | 
  728 | + Request (application/json)
  729 | 
  730 |     + Body
  731 | 
  732 |             {
  733 |                 "code": "fd0847dbb559752d932dd3c1ac34ff98d27b11fe2fea5a864f44740cd7919ad0",
  734 |                 "client_id": "9b36d8c0db59eff5038aea7a417d73e69aea75b41aac771816d2ef1b3109cc2f",
  735 |                 "client_secret": "d6ea27703957b69939b8104ed4524595e210cd2e79af587744a7eb6e58f5b3d2"
  736 |             }
  737 | 
  738 | + Response 200 (application/json)
  739 | 
  740 |     + Body
  741 | 
  742 |             {
  743 |                 "access_token": "dbaf9757982a9e738f05d249b7b5b4a266b3a139049317c4909f2f263572c781",
  744 |                 "token_type": "bearer",
  745 |                 "expires_in": 86400,
  746 |                 "refresh_token": "76ba4c5c75c96f6087f58a4de10be6c00b29ea1ddc3b2022ee2016d1363e3a7c",
  747 |                 "scope": "public",
  748 |                 "created_at": 1487889741
  749 |             }
  750 | 
  751 | # Group Calendars
  752 | By default, the calendar will return all shows or movies for the specified time period and can be global or user specific. The `start_date` defaults to today and `days` to 7. The maximum amount of `days` you can send is `33`. All dates (including the `start_date` and `first_aired`) are in UTC, so it's up to your app to handle any offsets based on the user's time zone.
  753 | 
  754 | The `my` calendar displays episodes for all shows that have been watched, collected, or watchlisted plus individual episodes on the watchlist. It will remove any shows that have been hidden from the calendar. The `all` calendar displays info for all shows airing during the specified period.
  755 |

 1854 | # Group Checkin
 1855 | Checking in is a manual action used by mobile apps allowing the user to indicate what they are watching right now. While not as effortless as scrobbling, checkins help fill in the gaps. You might be watching live tv, at a friend's house, or watching a movie in theaters. You can simply checkin from your phone or tablet in those situations. The item will display as *watching* on the site, then automatically switch to *watched* status once the duration has elapsed.
 1856 | 
 1857 | ## Checkin [/checkin]
 1858 | 
 1859 | ### Check into an item [POST]
 1860 | #### &#128274; OAuth Required
 1861 | Check into a movie or episode. This should be tied to a user action to manually indicate they are watching something. The item will display as *watching* on the site, then automatically switch to *watched* status once the duration has elapsed. A unique history `id` (64-bit integer) will be returned and can be used to reference this checkin directly.
 1862 | 
 1863 | #### JSON POST Data
 1864 | | Key | Type | Value |
 1865 | |---|---|---|
 1866 | | item <span style="color:red;">*</a> | object | `movie` or `episode` object. (see examples &#8594;) |
 1867 | | `sharing`  | object | Control sharing to any connected social networks. (see below &#8595;) |
 1868 | | `message`  | string | Message used for sharing. If not sent, it will use the watching string in the user settings. |
 1869 | 
 1870 | #### Sharing
 1871 | The `sharing` object is optional and will apply the user's settings if not sent. If `sharing` is sent, each key will override the user's setting for that social network. Send `true` to post or `false` to not post on the indicated social network. You can see which social networks a user has connected with the [**/users/settings**](/reference/users/settings) method.
 1872 | 
 1873 | | Key | Type |
 1874 | |---|---|
 1875 | | `twitter` | boolean |
 1876 | | `mastodon` | boolean |
 1877 | | `tumblr` | boolean |
 1878 | 
 1879 | > ### 🅽🅾🆃🅴
 1880 | > _If a checkin is already in progress, a `409` HTTP status code will returned. The response will contain an `expires_at` timestamp which is when the user can check in again._

 2159 | # Group Certifications
 2160 | 
 2161 | ## List [/certifications/{type}]

 2163 |

 2214 | # Group Comments
 2215 | Comments are attached to any movie, show, season, episode, or list and can be a quick shout or a more detailed review. Each comment can have replies and can be liked. These likes are used to determine popular comments. Comments must follow these rules and your app should indicate these to the user. Failure to adhere to these rules could suspend the user's commenting abilities.
 2216 | 
 2217 | - Comments must be at least 5 words.
 2218 | - Comments 200 words or longer will be automatically marked as a review.
 2219 | - Correctly indicate if the comment contains spoilers.
 2220 | - Only write comments in English - **This is important!**
 2221 | - **Do not include** app specific text like (via App Name) or #apphashtag. This clutters up the comments and failure to clean the comment text could get your app blacklisted from commenting.
 2222 | 
 2223 | #### Possible Error Responses
 2224 | 
 2225 | | Code | Description |
 2226 | |---|---|
 2227 | | `401` | Invalid user
 2228 | | `401` | User banned from commenting
 2229 | | `404` | Item not found or doesn't allow comments
 2230 | | `409` | Comment can't be deleted
 2231 | | `422` | Validation errors
 2232 | 
 2233 | #### Validation Errors
 2234 | 
 2235 | If a comment doesn't pass validation, it returns a `422` HTTP error code and an array of validation errors in the response. The validation errors could include:
 2236 | 
 2237 | | Error Message |
 2238 | |---|
 2239 | | `must be at least 5 words` |
 2240 | | `must be written in English` |
 2241 | 
 2242 | #### Comment Formatting
 2243 | 
 2244 | Comments support [**markdown**](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Markdown) formatting so you'll want to render this in your app so it matches what the website does. In addition, we support inline spoiler tags like `[spoiler]text[/spoiler]` which you should also handle independent of the top level `spoiler` attribute.
 2245 | 
 2246 | ## Comments [/comments]
 2247 | 
 2248 | ### Post a comment [POST]
 2249 | #### &#128274; OAuth Required &#128513; Emojis
 2250 | Add a new comment to a movie, show, season, episode, or list. Make sure to allow and encourage *spoilers* to be indicated in your app and follow the rules listed above.
 2251 | 
 2252 | #### JSON POST Data
 2253 | | Key | Type | Default | Value |
 2254 | |---|---|---|---|
 2255 | | item <span style="color:red;">*</a> | object | | `movie`, `show`, `season`, `episode`, or `list` object. (see examples &#8594;) |
 2256 | | `comment` <span style="color:red;">*</a> | string |  | Text for the comment. |
 2257 | | `spoiler` | boolean | `false` | Is this a spoiler? |
 2258 | | `sharing`  | object | | Control sharing to any connected social networks. (see below &#8595;) |
 2259 | 
 2260 | #### Sharing
 2261 | The `sharing` object is optional and will apply the user's settings if not sent. If `sharing` is sent, each key will override the user's setting for that social network. Send `true` to post or `false` to not post on the indicated social network. You can see which social networks a user has connected with the [**/users/settings**](/reference/users/settings) method.
 2262 | 
 2263 | | Key | Type |
 2264 | |---|---|
 2265 | | `twitter` | boolean |
 2266 | | `tumblr` | boolean |
 2267 | | `medium` | boolean |

 2551 | ## Comment [/comments/{id}]
 2552 | 
 2553 | + Parameters
 2554 |     + id (required, integer, `417`) ... A specific comment ID.
 2555 | 
 2556 | ### Get a comment or reply [GET]
 2557 | ####  &#128513; Emojis

 5319 | # Group Languages
 5320 | 
 5321 | ## List [/languages/{type}]
 5322 | Some API methods allow filtering by language code, so it's good to cache this list in your app.
 5323 | 
 5324 | + Parameters
 5325 |     + type (required, string, `movies`) ...
 5326 | 
 5327 |         + Values
 5328 |             + `movies`
 5329 |             + `shows`
 5330 | 
 5331 | ### Get languages [GET]
 5332 | Get a list of all langauges, including names and codes.
 5333 | 
 5334 | + Request (application/json)
 5335 | 
 5336 |     + Headers
 5337 | 
 5338 |             trakt-api-version: 2
 5339 |             trakt-api-key: [client_id]
 5340 | 
 5341 | + Response 200 (application/json)
 5342 | 
 5343 |     + Body
 5344 | 
 5345 |             [
 5346 |                 {
 5347 |                     "name": "English",
 5348 |                     "code": "en"
 5349 |                 },
 5350 |                 {
 5351 |                     "name": "Italian",
 5352 |                     "code": "it"
 5353 |                 },
 5354 |                 {
 5355 |                     "name": "Polish",
 5356 |                     "code": "pl"
 5357 |                 }
 5358 |             ]
 5359 | 
 5360 | ## Group Lists
 5361 | 
 5362 | ## Trending [/lists/trending/{type}]
 5363 | 
 5364 | + Parameters
 5365 |     + type (optional, string, `personal`) ...
 5366 | 
 5367 |         + Values
 5368 |             + `personal`
 5369 |             + `official`
 5370 | 
 5371 | ### Get trending lists [GET]
 5372 | #### &#128196; Pagination &#128513; Emojis
 5373 | 
 5374 | Returns all lists with the most likes and comments over the last 7 days.

 5376 | + Request (application/json)

 5378 |     + Headers

 5380 |             trakt-api-version: 2
 5381 |             trakt-api-key: [client_id]

 5383 | + Response 200 (application/json)
 5384 | 
 5385 |     + Headers
 5386 | 
 5387 |             X-Pagination-Page: 1
 5388 |             X-Pagination-Limit: 10
 5389 |             X-Pagination-Page-Count: 10
 5390 |             X-Pagination-Item-Count: 100

 5722 | 
 5723 | + Parameters

 5726 |

 5730 |             + `season`
 5731 |             + `episode`
 5732 |             + `person`
 5733 |

 5735 |

 5739 |             + `title`
 5740 |             + `released`
 5741 |             + `runtime`
 5742 |             + `popularity`

 5744 |             + `percentage`
 5745 |             + `imdb_rating`
 5746 |             + `tmdb_rating`
 5747 |             + `rt_tomatometer`
 5748 |             + `rt_audience`
 5749 |             + `metascore`
 5750 |             + `votes`
 5751 |             + `imdb_votes`
 5752 |             + `tmdb_votes`
 5753 |             + `my_rating`
 5754 |             + `watched`
 5755 |             + `collected`
 5756 | 
 5757 |     + sort_how (optional, string, `asc`) ... Sort direction
 5758 | 
 5759 |         + Values
 5760 |             + `asc`
 5761 |             + `desc`
 5762 | 
 5763 | ### Get items on a list [GET]
 5764 | #### 🔥 **VIP Enhanced** &#128196; Pagination Optional &#10024; Extended Info &#128513; Emojis
 5765 | Get all items on a personal list. Items can be a `movie`, `show`, `season`, `episode`, or `person`. You can optionally specify the `type` parameter with a single value or comma delimited string for multiple item types.
 5766 | 
 5767 | #### Notes
 5768 | 
 5769 | Each list item contains a `notes` field with text entered by the user.
 5770 | 
 5771 | #### Sorting
 5772 | 
 5773 | Default sorting is based on the list defaults and sent in the `X-Sort-By` and `X-Sort-How` headers. If you specify the `sort_by` and `sort_how` parameters, the response will be sorted based on those values and sent in the `X-Applied-Sort-By` and `X-Applied-Sort-How` headers.
 5774 | 
 5775 | Some `sort_by` options are 🔥 **VIP Only** including `imdb_rating`, `tmdb_rating`, `rt_tomatometer`, `rt_audience`, `metascore`, `votes`, `imdb_votes`, and `tmdb_votes`. If sent for a non VIP, the items will fall back to  `rank`.
 5776 | 
 5777 | + Request (application/json)
 5778 | 
 5779 |     + Headers
 5780 | 
 5781 |             trakt-api-version: 2
 5782 |             trakt-api-key: [client_id]
 5783 | 
 5784 | + Response 200 (application/json)
 5785 | 
 5786 |     + Headers
 5787 | 
 5788 |             X-Private-User: false
 5789 |             X-Sort-By: rank
 5790 |             X-Sort-How: asc
 5791 |             X-List-ID: 1

 7091 | ## Updates [/movies/updates/{start_date}]
 7092 | + Parameters
 7093 |     + start_date (optional, string, `2020-11-27T00:00:00Z`) ... Updated since this date and time.
 7094 | 
 7095 | ### Get recently updated movies [GET]
 7096 | #### &#128196; Pagination &#10024; Extended Info
 7097 | 
 7098 | Returns all movies updated since the specified UTC date and time. We recommended storing the `X-Start-Date` header you can be efficient using this method moving forward. By default, `10` results are returned. You can send a `limit` to get up to `100` results per page.
 7099 | 
 7100 | > ### ☣️ 🅸🅼🅿🅾🆁🆃🅰🅽🆃
 7101 | > _The `start_date` is only accurate to the hour, for caching purposes. Please drop the minutes and seconds from your timestamp to help optimize our cached data. For example, use `2021-07-17T12:00:00Z` and not `2021-07-17T12:23:34Z`._
 7102 | 
 7103 | > ### 🅽🅾🆃🅴
 7104 | > _The `start_date` can only be a maximum of 30 days in the past._
 7105 | 
 7106 | + Request (application/json)
 7107 | 
 7108 |     + Headers
 7109 | 
 7110 |             trakt-api-version: 2
 7111 |             trakt-api-key: [client_id]
 7112 | 
 7113 | + Response 200 (application/json)
 7114 | 
 7115 |     + Headers
 7116 | 
 7117 |             X-Start-Date: 2020-11-27T00:00:00Z
 7118 |             X-Pagination-Page: 1
 7119 |             X-Pagination-Limit: 10
 7120 |             X-Pagination-Page-Count: 10
 7121 |             X-Pagination-Item-Count: 100
 7122 |

 7355 | ### Get all movie releases [GET]
 7356 |

The release type can be set to `unknown`, `premiere`, `limited`, `theatrical`, `digital`, `physical`, or `tv`. The `note` might have optional info such as the film festival name for a `premiere` release or Blu-ray specs for a `physical` release.  7464 | ## Translations [/movies/{id}/translations/{language}]
 7465 | + Parameters
 7466 |     + id (required, string, `tron-legacy-2010`) ... Trakt ID, Trakt slug, or IMDB ID
 7467 |     + language (optional, string, `es`) ... 2 character language code
 7468 | 
 7469 | ### Get all movie translations [GET]
 7470 | 
 7471 | Returns all translations for a movie, including language and translated values for title, tagline and overview.
 7472 |

 7508 | ## Comments [/movies/{id}/comments/{sort}]
 7509 | + Parameters
 7510 |     + id (required, string, `tron-legacy-2010`) ... Trakt ID, Trakt slug, or IMDB ID
 7511 |     + sort (optional, string, `newest`) ... how to sort
 7512 | 
 7513 |         + Values
 7514 |             + `newest`
 7515 |             + `oldest`
 7516 |             + `likes`
 7517 |             + `replies`
 7518 |             + `highest`
 7519 |             + `lowest`
 7520 |             + `plays`
 7521 | 
 7522 | ### Get all movie comments [GET]
 7523 | #### &#128275; OAuth Optional &#128196; Pagination &#128513; Emojis
 7524 | 
 7525 | Returns all top level comments for a movie. By default, the `newest` comments are returned first. Other sorting options include `oldest`, most `likes`, most `replies`, `highest` rated, `lowest` rated, and most `plays`.
 7526 | 
 7527 | > ### 🅽🅾🆃🅴
 7528 | > _If you send OAuth, comments from blocked users will be automatically filtered out._
 7529 | 
 7530 | + Request (application/json)
 7531 | 
 7532 |     + Headers
 7533 | 
 7534 |             trakt-api-version: 2
 7535 |             trakt-api-key: [client_id]
 7536 | 
 7537 | + Response 200 (application/json)
 7538 | 
 7539 |     + Headers
 7540 | 
 7541 |             X-Pagination-Page: 1
 7542 |             X-Pagination-Limit: 10
 7543 |             X-Pagination-Page-Count: 10
 7544 |             X-Pagination-Item-Count: 100
 7545 | 
 7546 |     + Body
 7547 |

 7577 | ## Lists [/movies/{id}/lists/{type}/{sort}]
 7578 | + Parameters

 7589 |     + sort (optional, string, `popular`) ... How to sort
 7590 | 
 7591 |         + Values

 7596 |             + `added`
 7597 |             + `updated`

 7655 | ## People [/movies/{id}/people]
 7656 | + Parameters
 7657 |     + id (required, string, `tron-legacy-2010`) ... Trakt ID, Trakt slug, or IMDB ID
 7658 | 
 7659 | ### Get all people for a movie [GET]
 7660 | #### &#10024; Extended Info
 7661 | Returns all `cast` and `crew` for a movie. Each `cast` member will have a `characters` array and a standard `person` object.
 7662 | 
 7663 | The `crew` object will be broken up by department into `production`, `art`, `crew`, `costume & make-up`, `directing`, `writing`, `sound`, `camera`, `visual effects`, `lighting`, and `editing` (if there are people for those crew positions). Each of those members will have a `jobs` array and a standard `person` object.
 7664 | 
 7665 | + Request (application/json)
 7666 | 
 7667 |     + Headers
 7668 | 
 7669 |             trakt-api-version: 2
 7670 |             trakt-api-key: [client_id]
 7671 | 
 7672 | + Response 200 (application/json)

 8660 | # Group Networks
 8661 | 
 8662 | ## List [/networks]

 8706 | 
 8707 | # Group Notes
 8708 | Notes *(500 maximum characters)* attached to any `movie`, `show`, `season`, `episode`, or `person` and are only visible to the user who created them. They are also set to `private` and can't be marked as a `spoiler`. Notes attached to any `history`, `collection`, or `rating` can have their `privacy` and `spoiler` set.
 8709 | 
 8710 | #### Possible Error Responses
 8711 | 
 8712 | | Code | Description |
 8713 | |---|---|
 8714 | | `401` | Invalid user
 8715 | | `404` | Item not found or doesn't allow notes
 8716 | | `409` | Note can't be deleted
 8717 | | `422` | Validation errors
 8718 | 
 8719 | ## Notes [/notes]
 8720 | 
 8721 | ### Add notes [POST]
 8722 | #### 🔥 VIP Enhanced &#128274; OAuth Required &#128513; Emojis
 8723 | Notes *(500 maximum characters)* added to a `movie`, `show`, `season`, `episode`, or `person` will automatically be set to `private`. You can send just the media item.
 8724 | 
 8725 | Notes *(500 maximum characters)* added to a `history`, `collection`, or `rating` can have their `privacy` and `spoiler` set. You need to send the `attached_to` object so we know where to attach the note.
 8726 | 
 8727 | #### Limits
 8728 | 
 8729 | If the user's note limit is exceeded, a `420` HTTP error code is returned. Use the [**/users/settings**](/reference/users/settings) method to get all limits for a user account. Upgrading to [**Trakt VIP**](https://trakt.tv/vip) allows for unlimited notes.
 8730 | 
 8731 | #### JSON POST Data
 8732 | | Key | Type | Default | Value |
 8733 | |---|---|---|---|
 8734 | | item <span style="color:red;">*</a> | object | | `movie`, `show`, `season`, `episode`, `person`, 'history', 'collection', 'rating' object. (see examples &#8594;) |
 8735 | | `notes` <span style="color:red;">*</a> | string |  | Text for the notes. |
 8736 | | `spoiler` | boolean | `false` | Is this a spoiler? |
 8737 | | `privacy` | string | `private` | `private`, `friends`, `public` |
 8738 | 
 8739 | + Request (application/json)
 8740 | 
 8741 |     Movie note by sending a `movie` object.
 8742 | 
 8743 |     + Headers
 8744 | 
 8745 |             Authorization: Bearer [access_token]
 8746 |             trakt-api-version: 2
 8747 |             trakt-api-key: [client_id]
 8748 | 
 8749 |     + Body
 8750 | 
 8751 |             {
 8752 |                 "movie": {
 8753 |                     "title": "Guardians of the Galaxy",
 8754 |                     "year": 2014,
 8755 |                     "ids": {
 8756 |                         "trakt": 28,
 8757 |                         "slug": "guardians-of-the-galaxy-2014",
 8758 |                         "imdb": "tt2015381",
 8759 |                         "tmdb": 118340
 8760 |                     }
 8761 |                 },
 8762 |                 "notes": "Watch this in IMAX!"
 8763 |             }
 8764 |

 8776 |                 "user": {

 9161 | #### &#128274; OAuth Required &#128513; Emojis
 9162 | Update a single note *(500 maximum characters)*. The OAuth user must match the author of the note in order to update it. If not, a `401` HTTP status is returned.

 9166 | |---|---|---|---|

 9169 | | `privacy` | string | `private` | `private`, `friends`, `public` |

 9222 | ## Item [/notes/{id}/item]
 9223 | 
 9224 | + Parameters
 9225 |     + id (required, integer, `417`) ... A specific note ID.
 9226 | 
 9227 | ### Get the attached item [GET]
 9228 | 
 9229 | #### &#10024; Extended Info
 9230 | Returns the item this note is `attached_to`. Media items like `movie`, `show`, `season`, `episode`, or `person` are straightforward, but `history` will need to be mapped to that specific play in their watched history since they might have multiple plays. Since `collection` and `rating` is a 1:1 association, you can assume the note is attached to the media item in the `type` field that has been collected or rated.

 9290 | ## Updates [/people/updates/{start_date}]
 9291 | + Parameters
 9292 |     + start_date (optional, string, `2020-11-27T00:00:00Z`) ... Updated since this date and time.
 9293 | 
 9294 | ### Get recently updated people [GET]
 9295 | #### &#128196; Pagination &#10024; Extended Info
 9296 | 
 9297 | Returns all people updated since the specified UTC date and time. We recommended storing the `X-Start-Date` header you can be efficient using this method moving forward. By default, `10` results are returned. You can send a `limit` to get up to `100` results per page.
 9298 | 
 9299 | > ### ☣️ 🅸🅼🅿🅾🆁🆃🅰🅽🆃
 9300 | > _The `start_date` is only accurate to the hour, for caching purposes. Please drop the minutes and seconds from your timestamp to help optimize our cached data. For example, use `2021-07-17T12:00:00Z` and not `2021-07-17T12:23:34Z`._
 9301 | 
 9302 | > ### 🅽🅾🆃🅴
 9303 | > _The `start_date` can only be a maximum of 30 days in the past._

 9317 |             X-Pagination-Page: 1
 9318 |             X-Pagination-Limit: 10

 9320 |             X-Pagination-Item-Count: 100

 9392 | ## Summary [/people/{id}]
 9393 | + Parameters
 9394 |     + id (required, string, `bryan-cranston`) ... Trakt ID, Trakt slug, or IMDB ID
 9395 | 
 9396 | ### Get a single person [GET]
 9397 | #### &#10024; Extended Info
 9398 | Returns a single person's details.
 9399 | 
 9400 | #### Gender
 9401 | If available, the `gender` property will be set to `male`, `female`, or `non_binary`.
 9402 | 
 9403 | #### Known For Department
 9404 | If available, the `known_for_department` property will be set to `production`, `art`, `crew`, `costume & make-up`, `directing`, `writing`, `sound`, `camera`, `visual effects`, `lighting`, or `editing`. Many people have credits across departments, `known_for` allows you to select their default credits more accurately.

 9410 |             trakt-api-version: 2

 9417 |     ```

 9463 | ## Movies [/people/{id}/movies]

Each of those members will have a `jobs` array and a standard `movie` object.

 9550 | + Parameters
 9551 |     + id (required, string, `bryan-cranston`) ... Trakt ID, Trakt slug, or IMDB ID
 9552 | 
 9553 | ### Get show credits [GET]
 9554 | #### &#10024; Extended Info
 9555 | Returns all shows where this person is in the `cast` or `crew`, including the `episode_count` for which they appear. Each `cast` object will have a `characters` array and a standard `show` object. If `series_regular` is `true`, this person is a series regular and not simply a guest star.
 9556 | 
 9557 | The `crew` object will be broken up by department into `production`, `art`, `crew`, `costume & make-up`, `directing`, `writing`, `sound`, `camera`, `visual effects`, `lighting`, `editing`, and `created  by` (if there are people for those crew positions). Each of those members will have a `jobs` array and a standard `show` object.
 9558 |

 9685 | ## Refresh [/people/{id}/refresh]
 9686 | 
 9687 | + Parameters
 9688 |     + id (required, string, `bryan-cranston`) ... Trakt ID, Trakt slug, or IMDB ID
 9689 | 
 9690 | ### Refresh person metadata [POST]
 9691 | #### 🔥 VIP Only &#128274; OAuth Required
 9692 | Queue this person for a full metadata and image refresh. It might take up to 8 hours for the updated metadata to be availabe through the API.
 9693 | 
 9694 | > ### 🅽🅾🆃🅴
 9695 | > _If this person is already queued, a `409` HTTP status code will returned._
 9696 | 
 9697 | + Request (application/json)
 9698 | 
 9699 |     + Headers
 9700 | 
 9701 |             Authorization: Bearer [access_token]
 9702 |             trakt-api-version: 2
 9703 |             trakt-api-key: [client_id]
 9704 | 
 9705 | + Response 201 (application/json)
 9706 | 
 9707 | # Group Recommendations
 9708 | Trakt recommendations are built on top of your viewing activity and preferences. The more you watch, the better your recommendations will be. We also use other factors for the algorithm to further personalize what gets recommended.
 9709 |

10103 | ## Hide Show [/recommendations/shows/{id}]
10104 | 
10105 | + Parameters
10106 |     + id (required, string, `922`) ... Trakt ID, Trakt slug, or IMDB ID
10107 | 
10108 | ### Hide a show recommendation [DELETE]
10109 | #### &#128274; OAuth Required
10110 | Hide a show from getting recommended anymore.
10111 | 
10112 | + Request (application/json)
10113 | 
10114 |     + Headers
10115 | 
10116 |             Authorization: Bearer [access_token]
10117 |             trakt-api-version: 2
10118 |             trakt-api-key: [client_id]
10119 | 
10120 | + Response 204
10121 | 
10122 | # Group Scrobble
10123 | Scrobbling is an automatic way to track what a user is watching in a media center. The media center should send events that correspond to starting, pausing, and stopping (or finishing) watching a movie or episode.
10124 | 
10125 | ## Start [/scrobble/start]
10126 | 
10127 | ### Start watching in a media center [POST]
10128 | #### &#128274; OAuth Required
10129 | Use this method when the video initially starts playing or is unpaused. This will remove any playback progress if it exists.
10130 | 
10131 | > ### 🅽🅾🆃🅴
10132 | > _A watching status will auto expire after the remaining runtime has elapsed. There is no need to call this method again while continuing to watch the same item._
10133 | 
10134 | #### JSON POST Data
10135 | | Key | Type | Value |
10136 | |---|---|---|
10137 | | item <span style="color:red;">*</a> | object | `movie` or `episode` object. (see examples &#8594;) |
10138 | | `progress` <span style="color:red;">*</a> | float | Progress percentage between 0 and 100. |
10139 | 
10140 | + Request (application/json)
10141 | 
10142 |     Start watching a movie by sending a standard `movie` object.
10143 | 
10144 |     + Headers
10145 | 
10146 |             Authorization: Bearer [access_token]
10147 |             trakt-api-version: 2
10148 |             trakt-api-key: [client_id]
10149 | 
10150 |     + Body
10151 | 
10152 |             {
10153 |                 "movie": {
10154 |                     "title": "Guardians of the Galaxy",
10155 |                     "year": 2014,
10156 |                     "ids": {
10157 |                         "trakt": 28,
10158 |                         "slug": "guardians-of-the-galaxy-2014",
10159 |                         "imdb": "tt2015381",
10160 |                         "tmdb": 118340
10161 |                     }
10162 |                 },
10163 |                 "progress": 1.25
10164 |             }
10165 | 
10166 | + Response 201 (application/json)
10167 | 
10168 |     + Body
10169 | 
10170 |             {
10171 |                 "id": 0,
10172 |                 "action": "start",
10173 |                 "progress": 1.25,
10174 |                 "sharing": {
10175 |                     "twitter": true,
10176 |                     "mastodon": true,
10177 |                     "tumblr": false
10178 |                 },
10179 |                 "movie": {
10180 |                     "title": "Guardians of the Galaxy",
10181 |                     "year": 2014,
10182 |                     "ids": {
10183 |                         "trakt": 28,
10184 |                         "slug": "guardians-of-the-galaxy-2014",
10185 |                         "imdb": "tt2015381",
10186 |                         "tmdb": 118340
10187 |                     }
10188 |                 }
10189 |             }
10190 |

10192 | 
10193 |     Start watching an episode by sending a standard `episode` object.
10194 | 
10195 |     + Headers
10196 | 
10197 |             Authorization: Bearer [access_token]
10198 |             trakt-api-version: 2
10199 |             trakt-api-key: [client_id]
10200 |

10382 | ## Pause [/scrobble/pause]
10383 | 
10384 | ### Pause watching in a media center [POST]
10385 | #### &#128274; OAuth Required
10386 | Use this method when the video is paused. The playback progress will be saved and [**/sync/playback**](/reference/sync/playback/) can be used to resume the video from this exact position. Unpause a video by calling the [**/scrobble/start**](/reference/scrobble/start/) method again.
10387 | 
10388 | #### JSON POST Data
10389 | | Key | Type | Value |
10390 | |---|---|---|
10391 | | item <span style="color:red;">*</a> | object | `movie` or `episode` object. (see examples &#8594;) |
10392 | | `progress` <span style="color:red;">*</a> | float | Progress percentage between 0 and 100. |
10393 | 
10394 | + Request (application/json)
10395 | 
10396 |     + Headers
10397 | 
10398 |             Authorization: Bearer [access_token]
10399 |             trakt-api-version: 2
10400 |             trakt-api-key: [client_id]
10401 | 
10402 |     + Body

10443 | ## Stop [/scrobble/stop]
10444 | 
10445 | ### Stop or finish watching in a media center [POST]
10446 | #### &#128274; OAuth Required
10447 | Use this method when the video is stopped or finishes playing on its own. If the progress is above 80%, the video will be scrobbled and the `action` will be set to **scrobble**. A unique history `id` (64-bit integer) will be returned and can be used to reference this `scrobble` directly.
10448 | 
10449 | If the progress is less than 80%, it will be treated as a *pause* and the `action` will be set to **pause**. The playback progress will be saved and [**/sync/playback**](/reference/sync/playback/) can be used to resume the video from this exact position.
10450 | 
10451 | > ### 🅽🅾🆃🅴
10452 | > _If you prefer to use a threshold higher than 80%, you should use [**/scrobble/pause**](/reference/scrobble/pause/) yourself so it doesn't create duplicate scrobbles._
10453 | 
10454 | #### JSON POST Data
10455 | | Key | Type | Value |
10456 | |---|---|---|
10457 | | item <span style="color:red;">*</a> | object | `movie` or `episode` object. (see examples &#8594;) |
10458 | | `progress` <span style="color:red;">*</a> | flloat | Progress percentage between 0 and 100. |
10459 | 
10460 | > ### 🅽🅾🆃🅴
10461 | > _If the same item was just scrobbled, a `409` HTTP status code will returned to avoid scrobbling a duplicate. The response will contain a `watched_at` timestamp when the item was last scrobbled and a `expires_at` timestamp when the item can be scrobbled again._
10462 |

10767 | # Group Search
10768 | 
10769 | Searches can use queries or ID lookups. Queries will search text fields like the title and overview. ID lookups are helpful if you have an external ID and want to get the Trakt ID and info. These methods can search for movies, shows, episodes, people, and lists.
10770 | 
10771 | ## Text Query [/search/{type}{?query}]
10772 | 
10773 | + Parameters
10774 | 
10775 |     + type (required, string, `movie`) ... Search type.
10776 | 
10777 |       + Values
10778 |           + `movie`
10779 |           + `show`
10780 |           + `episode`
10781 |           + `person`
10782 |           + `list`
10783 | 
10784 |     + query (required, string, `tron`) ... Search all text based fields.
10785 | 
10786 |     + fields (optional, string, `title`) ... Specific text fields.
10787 | 
10788 |       + Values
10789 |           + `title`
10790 |           + `tagline`
10791 |           + `overview`
10792 |           + `people`
10793 |           + `translations`
10794 |           + `aliases`
10795 |           + `name`
10796 |           + `biography`
10797 |           + `description`
10798 | 
10799 | ### Get text query results [GET]
10800 | #### &#128196; Pagination &#10024; Extended Info &#127898; Filters
10801 | 
10802 | Search all text fields that a media object contains (i.e. title, overview, etc). Results are ordered by the most relevant score. Specify the `type` of results by sending a single value or a comma delimited string for multiple types.
10803 | 
10804 | #### Special Characters
10805 | 
10806 | Our search engine gives the following characters special meaning when they appear in a query:
10807 | 
10808 | `+ - && || ! ( ) { } [ ] ^ " ~ * ? : /`
10809 | 
10810 | To interpret any of these characters literally (and not as a special character), precede the character with a backslash `\` character.
10811 | 
10812 | #### Search Fields
10813 | 
10814 | By default, certain text fields are used to search for the `query`. You can optionally specify the `fields` parameter with a single value or comma delimited string for multiple fields. Each `type` has specific `fields` that can be specified. This can be useful if you want to support more strict searches (i.e. title only).
10815 | 
10816 | | Type | Field | Default |
10817 | |---|---|---|
10818 | | `movie` | `title` | &#10003; |
10819 | |  | `original_title` | &#10003; |
10820 | |  | `translations` | &#10003; |
10821 | |  | `aliases` | &#10003; |
10822 | |  | `tagline` | |
10823 | |  | `overview` | |
10824 | |  | `people` | |
10825 | | `show` | `title` | &#10003; |
10826 | |  | `original_title` | &#10003; |
10827 | |  | `translations` | &#10003; |
10828 | |  | `aliases` | &#10003; |
10829 | |  | `overview` | |
10830 | |  | `people` | |
10831 | | `episode` | `title` | &#10003; |
10832 | |  | `show_title` | &#10003; |
10833 | |  | `overview` | |
10834 | | `person` | `name` | &#10003; |
10835 | |  | `biography` | |
10836 | | `list` | `name` | &#10003; |
10837 | |  | `description` | &#10003; |
10838 | 
10839 | + Request (application/json)
10840 | 
10841 |     + Headers
10842 | 
10843 |             trakt-api-version: 2
10844 |             trakt-api-key: [client_id]
10845 | 
10846 | + Response 200 (application/json)
10847 | 
10848 |     ```
10849 |     /search/movie,show,episode,person,list?query=tron
10850 |     ```

10966 | ## ID Lookup [/search/{id_type}/{id}{?type}]
10967 | + Parameters
10968 | 
10969 |     + id_type (required, string, `imdb`) ... Type of ID to lookup.
10970 | 
10971 |       + Values
10972 |           + `trakt`
10973 |           + `imdb`
10974 |           + `tmdb`
10975 |           + `tvdb`
10976 | 
10977 |     + id (required, string, `tt0848228`) ... ID that matches with the type.
10978 | 
10979 |     + type (optional, string, `movie`) ... Search type.
10980 | 
10981 |       + Values
10982 |           + `movie`
10983 |           + `show`
10984 |           + `episode`
10985 |           + `person`
10986 |           + `list`
10987 | 
10988 | ### Get ID lookup results [GET]
10989 | #### &#128196; Pagination &#10024; Extended Info
10990 | 
10991 | Lookup items by their Trakt, IMDB, TMDB, or TVDB ID. If you use the search url without a `type` it might return multiple items if the `id_type` is not globally unique. Specify the `type` of results by sending a single value or a comma delimited string for multiple types.
10992 | 
10993 | | Type | URL |
10994 | |---|---|
10995 | | `trakt` | `/search/trakt/:id` |
10996 | |  | `/search/trakt/:id?type=movie` |
10997 | |  | `/search/trakt/:id?type=show` |
10998 | |  | `/search/trakt/:id?type=episode` |
10999 | |  | `/search/trakt/:id?type=person` |
11000 | | `imdb` | `/search/imdb/:id` |
11001 | | `tmdb` | `/search/tmdb/:id` |
11002 | |  | `/search/tmdb/:id?type=movie` |
11003 | |  | `/search/tmdb/:id?type=show` |
11004 | |  | `/search/tmdb/:id?type=episode` |
11005 | |  | `/search/tmdb/:id?type=person` |
11006 | | `tvdb` | `/search/tvdb/:id` |
11007 | |  | `/search/tvdb/:id?type=show` |
11008 | |  | `/search/tvdb/:id?type=episode` |
11009 | 
11010 | + Request (application/json)
11011 | 
11012 |     + Headers
11013 | 
11014 |             trakt-api-version: 2
11015 |             trakt-api-key: [client_id]
11016 | 
11017 | + Response 200 (application/json)
11018 | 
11019 |     ```
11020 |     /search/trakt/12601?type=movie
11021 |     /search/imdb/tt1104001
11022 |     ```
11023 | 
11024 |     + Headers
11025 | 
11026 |             X-Pagination-Page: 1
11027 |             X-Pagination-Limit: 10
11028 |             X-Pagination-Page-Count: 1
11029 |             X-Pagination-Item-Count: 1
11030 | 
11031 |     + Body
11032 | 
11033 |             [
11034 |                 {
11035 |                     "type": "movie",
11036 |                     "score": null,

12105 | ## Updates [/shows/updates/{start_date}]
12106 | + Parameters
12107 |     + start_date (optional, string, `2020-11-27T00:00:00Z`) ... Updated since this date and time.
12108 | 
12109 | ### Get recently updated shows [GET]
12110 | #### &#128196; Pagination &#10024; Extended Info
12111 | 
12112 | Returns all shows updated since the specified UTC date and time. We recommended storing the `X-Start-Date` header you can be efficient using this method moving forward. By default, `10` results are returned. You can send a `limit` to get up to `100` results per page.
12113 | 
12114 | > ### ☣️ 🅸🅼🅿🅾🆁🆃🅰🅽🆃
12115 | > _The `start_date` is only accurate to the hour, for caching purposes. Please drop the minutes and seconds from your timestamp to help optimize our cached data. For example, use `2021-07-17T12:00:00Z` and not `2021-07-17T12:23:34Z`._
12116 | 
12117 | > ### 🅽🅾🆃🅴
12118 | > _The `start_date` can only be a maximum of 30 days in the past._
12119 | 
12120 | + Request (application/json)
12121 | 
12122 |     + Headers
12123 | 
12124 |             trakt-api-version: 2
12125 |             trakt-api-key: [client_id]
12126 | 
12127 | + Response 200 (application/json)
12128 | 
12129 |     + Headers
12130 | 
12131 |             X-Start-Date: 2020-11-27T00:00:00Z
12132 |             X-Pagination-Page: 1
12133 |             X-Pagination-Limit: 10
12134 |             X-Pagination-Page-Count: 10
12135 |             X-Pagination-Item-Count: 100
12136 | 
12137 |     + Body
12138 |

12211 | ## Summary [/shows/{id}]
12212 | + Parameters
12213 |     + id (required, string, `game-of-thrones`) ... Trakt ID, Trakt slug, or IMDB ID
12214 | 
12215 | ### Get a single show [GET]
12216 | #### &#10024; Extended Info
12217 | Returns a single shows's details. If you request extended info, the `airs` object is relative to the show's country. You can use the `day`, `time`, and `timezone` to construct your own date then convert it to whatever timezone your user is in.
12218 | 
12219 | > ### 🅽🅾🆃🅴
12220 | > _When getting `full` extended info, the `status` field can have a value of `returning series` (airing right now),  `continuing` (airing right now), `in production` (airing soon), `planned` (in development), `upcoming` (in development),  `pilot`, `canceled`, or `ended`._
12221 | 
12222 | + Request (application/json)
12223 | 
12224 |     + Headers
12225 | 
12226 |             trakt-api-version: 2
12227 |             trakt-api-key: [client_id]
12228 | 
12229 | + Response 200 (application/json)
12230 | 
12231 |     ```
12232 |     /shows/game-of-thrones
12233 |     ```

12589 | ## Collection Progress [/shows/{id}/progress/collection{?hidden,specials,count_specials,last_activity}]
12590 | + Parameters
12591 |     + id (required, string, `game-of-thrones`) ... Trakt ID, Trakt slug, or IMDB ID
12592 |     + hidden (optional, string, `false`) ... include any hidden seasons
12593 |     + specials (optional, string, `false`) ... include specials as season 0
12594 |     + count_specials (optional, string, `true`) ... count specials in the overall stats (only applies if specials are included)
12595 |     + last_activity (optional, string, `aired`) ... used to calculate last_episode and next_episode
12596 | 
12597 |         + Values
12598 |             + `aired`
12599 |             + `collected`
12600 | 
12601 | ### Get show collection progress [GET]
12602 | #### &#128274; OAuth Required
12603 | Returns collection progress for a show including details on all aired seasons and episodes. The `next_episode` will be the next episode the user should collect, if there are no upcoming episodes it will be set to `null`.
12604 | 
12605 | By default, any hidden seasons will be removed from the response and stats. To include these and adjust the completion stats, set the `hidden` flag to `true`.
12606 | 
12607 | By default, specials will be excluded from the response. Set the `specials` flag to `true` to include season 0 and adjust the stats accordingly. If you'd like to include specials, but not adjust the stats, set `count_specials` to `false`.
12608 | 
12609 | By default, the `last_episode` and `next_episode` are calculated using the last `aired` episode the user has collected, even if they've collected older episodes more recently. To use their last collected episode for these calculations, set the `last_activity` flag to `collected`.
12610 | 
12611 | > ### 🅽🅾🆃🅴
12612 | > _Only aired episodes are used to calculate progress. Episodes in the future or without an air date are ignored._
12613 | 
12614 | + Request (application/json)
12615 | 
12616 |     + Headers
12617 | 
12618 |             Authorization: Bearer [access_token]
12619 |             trakt-api-version: 2
12620 |             trakt-api-key: [client_id]
12621 | 
12622 | + Response 200 (application/json)

12714 | ## Watched Progress [/shows/{id}/progress/watched{?hidden,specials,count_specials,last_activity}]
12715 | + Parameters
12716 |     + id (required, string, `game-of-thrones`) ... Trakt ID, Trakt slug, or IMDB ID
12717 |     + hidden (optional, string, `false`) ... include any hidden seasons
12718 |     + specials (optional, string, `false`) ... include specials as season 0
12719 |     + count_specials (optional, string, `true`) ... count specials in the overall stats (only applies if specials are included)

12725 | 
12726 | ### Get show watched progress [GET]
12727 | #### &#128274; OAuth Required
12728 | Returns watched progress for a show including details on all aired seasons and episodes. The `next_episode` will be the next episode the user should watch, if there are no upcoming episodes it will be set to `null`. If not `null`, the `reset_at` date is when the user started re-watching the show. Your app can adjust the progress by ignoring episodes with a `last_watched_at` prior to the `reset_at`.
12729 | 
12730 | By default, any hidden seasons will be removed from the response and stats. To include these and adjust the completion stats, set the `hidden` flag to `true`.
12731 | 
12732 | By default, specials will be excluded from the response. Set the `specials` flag to `true` to include season 0 and adjust the stats accordingly. If you'd like to include specials, but not adjust the stats, set `count_specials` to `false`.
12733 | 
12734 | By default, the `last_episode` and `next_episode` are calculated using the last `aired` episode the user has watched, even if they've watched older episodes more recently. To use their last watched episode for these calculations, set the `last_activity` flag to `watched`.
12735 | 
12736 | > ### 🅽🅾🆃🅴
12737 | > _Only aired episodes are used to calculate progress. Episodes in the future or without an air date are ignored._
12738 |

12743 |             Authorization: Bearer [access_token]

12880 | ## People [/shows/{id}/people]
12881 | + Parameters
12882 |     + id (required, string, `game-of-thrones`) ... Trakt ID, Trakt slug, or IMDB ID
12883 | 
12884 | ### Get all people for a show [GET]
12885 | #### &#10024; Extended Info
12886 | Returns all `cast` and `crew` for a show, including the `episode_count` for which they appears. Each `cast` member will have a `characters` array and a standard `person` object. 
12887 | 
12888 | The `crew` object will be broken up by department into `production`, `art`, `crew`, `costume & make-up`, `directing`, `writing`, `sound`, `camera`, `visual effects`, `lighting`, `editing`, and `created  by` (if there are people for those crew positions). Each of those members will have a `jobs` array and a standard `person` object.
12889 | 
12890 | #### Guest Stars
12891 | If you add `?extended=guest_stars` to the URL, it will return all guest stars that appeared in at least 1 episode of the show.
12892 | 
12893 | > ### 🅽🅾🆃🅴
12894 | > _This returns a lot of data, so please only use this extended parameter if you actually need it!_
12895 | 
12896 | + Request (application/json)
12897 | 
12898 |     + Headers
12899 | 
12900 |             trakt-api-version: 2
12901 |             trakt-api-key: [client_id]
12902 | 
12903 | + Response 200 (application/json)
12904 | 
12905 |     ```
12906 |     /shows/game-of-thrones/people
12907 |     ```
12908 |

13764 | ## Refresh [/shows/{id}/refresh]
13765 | 
13766 | + Parameters
13767 |     + id (required, string, `game-of-thrones`) ... Trakt ID, Trakt slug, or IMDB ID
13768 | 
13769 | ### Refresh show metadata [POST]
13770 | #### 🔥 VIP Only &#128274; OAuth Required
13771 | Queue this show for a full metadata and image refresh. It might take up to 8 hours for the updated metadata to be availabe through the API.
13772 | 
13773 | > ### 🅽🅾🆃🅴
13774 | > _If this show is already queued, a `409` HTTP status code will returned._
13775 | 
13776 | + Request (application/json)
13777 | 
13778 |     + Headers
13779 | 
13780 |             Authorization: Bearer [access_token]
13781 |             trakt-api-version: 2
13782 |             trakt-api-key: [client_id]
13783 | 
13784 | + Response 201 (application/json)
13785 | 
13786 | # Group Seasons

14598 |

14654 | ## Episodes [/shows/{id}/seasons/{season}{?translations}]

14659 |     + translations (optional, string, `es`) ... include episode translations
14660 |

14664 | 
14665 | #### Translations
14666 | If you'd like to included translated episode titles and overviews in the response, include the `translations` parameter in the URL. Include all languages by setting the parameter to `all` or use a specific 2 digit country language code to further limit it.

14795 | ## Translations [/shows/{id}/seasons/{season}/translations/{language}]
14796 | + Parameters

14801 | ### Get all season translations [GET]
14802 | 
14803 | Returns all translations for an season, including language and translated values for title and overview.

14805 | + Request (application/json)

14809 |             trakt-api-version: 2

14813 | 
14814 |     + Body

14817 |                 {
14818 |                     "title": "시즌 1",
14819 |                     "overview": "웨스테로스 북부 지방 윈터펠을 다스리는 에다드 스타크. 스타크 가문은 '겨울이 오고 있다'를 가언으로 몇 년, 때론 남은 일생 동안 계속 될지도 모르는 혹독한 겨울을 대비하며 지낸다. 그러던 중 에다드는 현재 왕좌에 있는 바라테온 가문의 로버트 왕의 핸드로서 왕을 보좌하기 위해 수도 킹스랜딩에 오게 된다. 바라테온 가문과 라니스터 가문, 왕좌를 빼앗긴 타르가옌 가문 등 칠왕국 안의 가문들은 욕망과 명예를 향한 열망으로 피 튀기는 암투를 시작하는데...",

14825 |                     "overview": "Het eerste seizoen van de epische fantasy tv- drama-serie Game of Thrones ging in première op HBO op 17 april 2011 en eindigde op 19 juni 2011, uitgezonden in de Verenigde Staten . Het bestaat uit 10 afleveringen , elke aflevering duurt ongeveer 55 minuten. Game of Thrones is gebaseerd op de roman A Game of Thrones , de eerste vermelding in Een Lied van IJs en Vuur serie van George RR Martin . Het verhaal speelt zich af in een fictieve wereld , in de eerste plaats op een continent genaamd Westeros . The Noble House Stark , onder leiding van Lord Eddard \" Ned \" Stark wordt betrokken in regelingen tegen koning Robert Baratheon wanneer de Hand van de Koning Jon Arryn op mysterieuze wijze sterft .",

14837 | ## Comments [/shows/{id}/seasons/{season}/comments/{sort}]
14838 | + Parameters

14841 |     + sort (optional, string, `newest`) ... how to sort

14846 |             + `likes`

14848 |             + `highest`

14853 | ### Get all season comments [GET]
14854 | #### &#128275; OAuth Optional &#128196; Pagination &#128513; Emojis
14855 | 
14856 | Returns all top level comments for a season. By default, the `newest` comments are returned first. Other sorting options include `oldest`, most `likes`, most `replies`, `highest` rated, `lowest` rated, most `plays`, and highest `watched` percentage.
14857 | 
14858 | > ### 🅽🅾🆃🅴
14859 | > _If you send OAuth, comments from blocked users will be automatically filtered out._
14860 | 
14861 | + Request (application/json)
14862 | 
14863 |     + Headers
14864 | 
14865 |             trakt-api-version: 2
14866 |             trakt-api-key: [client_id]
14867 | 
14868 | + Response 200 (application/json)
14869 | 
14870 |     + Headers
14871 | 
14872 |             X-Pagination-Page: 1
14873 |             X-Pagination-Limit: 10

14986 | ## People [/shows/{id}/seasons/{season}/people]
14987 | + Parameters
14988 |     + id (required, string, `game-of-thrones`) ... Trakt ID, Trakt slug, or IMDB ID
14989 |     + season (required, integer, `1`) ... season number
14990 | 
14991 | ### Get all people for a season [GET]
14992 | #### &#10024; Extended Info
14993 | Returns all `cast` and `crew` for a season, including the `episode_count` for which they appear. Each `cast` member will have a `characters` array and a standard `person` object. 
14994 | 
14995 | The `crew` object will be broken up by department into `production`, `art`, `crew`, `costume & make-up`, `directing`, `writing`, `sound`, `camera`, `visual effects`, `lighting`, and `editing` (if there are people for those crew positions).. Each of those members will have a `jobs` array and a standard `person` object.
14996 | 
14997 | #### Guest Stars
14998 | If you add `?extended=guest_stars` to the URL, it will return all guest stars that appeared in at least 1 episode of the season.
14999 | 
15000 | > ### 🅽🅾🆃🅴
15001 | > _This returns a lot of data, so please only use this extended parameter if you actually need it!_
15002 |

15005 |     + Headers

15008 |             trakt-api-key: [client_id]

15561 | ## Summary [/shows/{id}/seasons/{season}/episodes/{episode}]
15562 | 
15563 | + Parameters
15564 |     + id (required, string, `game-of-thrones`) ... Trakt ID, Trakt slug, or IMDB ID
15565 |     + season (required, integer, `1`) ... season number
15566 |     + episode (required, integer, `1`) ... episode number
15567 | 
15568 | ### Get a single episode for a show [GET]
15569 | #### &#10024; Extended Info
15570 | Returns a single episode's details. All date and times are in UTC and were calculated using the episode's `air_date` and show's `country` and `air_time`.
15571 | 
15572 | > ### 🅽🅾🆃🅴
15573 | > _If the `first_aired` is unknown, it will be set to `null`._
15574 | 
15575 | > ### 🅽🅾🆃🅴
15576 | > _When getting `full` extended info, the `episode_type` field can have a value of `standard`, `series_premiere` (season 1, episode 1), `season_premiere` (episode 1), `mid_season_finale`, `mid_season_premiere` (the next episode after the mid season finale), `season_finale`, or `series_finale` (last episode to air for an ended show)._
15577 | 
15578 | + Request (application/json)
15579 | 
15580 |     + Headers
15581 | 
15582 |             trakt-api-version: 2
15583 |             trakt-api-key: [client_id]
15584 | 
15585 | + Response 200 (application/json)
15586 | 
15587 |     ```
15588 |     /shows/game-of-thrones/seasons/1/episodes/1
15589 |     ```
15590 | 
15591 |     + Body
15592 | 
15593 |             {
15594 |                 "season": 1,
15595 |                 "number": 1,
15596 |                 "title": "Winter Is Coming",
15597 |                 "ids": {
15598 |                     "trakt": 36440,
15599 |                     "tvdb": 3254641,
15600 |                     "imdb": "tt1480055",
15601 |                     "tmdb": 63056
15602 |                 }
15603 |             }
15604 | 
15605 | + Response 200 (application/json)
15606 |

15829 | ## People [/shows/{id}/seasons/{season}/episodes/{episode}/people]
15830 | + Parameters
15831 |     + id (required, string, `game-of-thrones`) ... Trakt ID, Trakt slug, or IMDB ID
15832 |     + season (required, integer, `1`) ... season number
15833 |     + episode (required, integer, `1`) ... episode number
15834 | 
15835 | ### Get all people for an episode [GET]
15836 | #### &#10024; Extended Info
15837 | Returns all `cast` and `crew` for an episode. Each `cast` member will have a `characters` array and a standard `person` object. 
15838 | 
15839 | The `crew` object will be broken up by department into `production`, `art`, `crew`, `costume & make-up`, `directing`, `writing`, `sound`, `camera`, `visual effects`, `lighting`, and `editing` (if there are people for those crew positions). Each of those members will have a `jobs` array and a standard `person` object.
15840 | 
15841 | #### Guest Stars
15842 | If you add `?extended=guest_stars` to the URL, it will return all guest stars that appeared in the episode.
15843 | 
15844 | > ### 🅽🅾🆃🅴
15845 | > _This returns a lot of data, so please only use this extended parameter if you actually need it!_

15850 | 
15851 |             trakt-api-version: 2
15852 |             trakt-api-key: [client_id]
15853 |

16276 | # Group Sync
16277 | Syncing with trakt opens up quite a few cool features. Most importantly, trakt can serve as a cloud based backup for the data in your app. This is especially useful when rebuilding a media center or installing a mobile app on your new phone. It can also be nice to sync up multiple media centers with a central trakt account. If everything is in sync, your media can be managed from trakt and be reflected in your apps.
16278 | 
16279 | ### Media objects for syncing
16280 | As a baseline, all *add* and *remove* sync methods accept arrays of `movies`, `shows`, and `episodes`. Each of these top level array elements should themselves be an array of standard `movie`, `show`, or `episode` objects. Full examples are in the intro section called **Standard Media Objects**. Keep in mind that `episode` objects really only need the `ids` so it can find an exact match. This is useful for absolute ordered shows. Some methods also have optional metadata you can attach, so check the docs for each specific method.
16281 | 
16282 | Media objects will be matched by ID first, then fall back to title and year. IDs will be matched in this order `trakt`, `imdb`, `tmdb`, `tvdb`, and `slug`. If nothing is found, it will match on the `title` and `year`. If still nothing, it would use just the `title` (or `name` for people) and find the most current object that exists.
16283 | 
16284 | ### Watched History Sync
16285 | This is a 2 way sync that will get items from trakt to sync locally, plus find anything new and sync back to trakt. Perform this sync on startup or at set intervals (i.e. once every day) to keep everything in sync. *This will only send data to trakt and not remove it.*
16286 | 
16287 | ### Collection Sync
16288 | It's very handy to have a snapshot on trakt of everything you have available to watch locally. Syncing your local connection will do just that. *This will only send data to trakt and not remove it.*
16289 | 
16290 | ### Clean Collection
16291 | Cleaning a collection involves comparing the trakt collection to what exists locally. This will remove items from the trakt collection if they don't exist locally anymore. You should make this clear to the user that data might be removed from trakt.
16292 | 
16293 | ## Last Activities [/sync/last_activities]
16294 | 
16295 | ### Get last activity [GET]
16296 | 
16297 | #### &#128274; OAuth Required
16298 | This method is a useful first step in the syncing process. We recommended caching these dates locally, then you can compare to know exactly what data has changed recently. This can greatly optimize your syncs so you don't pull down a ton of data only to see nothing has actually changed.
16299 | 
16300 | #### Account
16301 | 
16302 | `settings_at` is set when the OAuth user updates any of their Trakt settings on the website. `followed_at` is set when another Trakt user follows or unfollows the OAuth user. `following_at` is set when the OAuth user follows or unfollows another Trakt user. `pending_at` is set when the OAuth user follows a private account, which requires their approval. `requested_at` is set when the OAuth user has a private account and someone requests to follow them.
16303 | 
16304 | + Request (application/json)
16305 | 
16306 |     + Headers
16307 | 
16308 |             Authorization: Bearer [access_token]
16309 |             trakt-api-version: 2
16310 |             trakt-api-key: [client_id]
16311 |

16380 | ## Playback [/sync/playback/{type}{?start_at,end_at}]
16381 | + Parameters
16382 |     + type (optional, string, `movies`) ...
16383 | 
16384 |         + Values
16385 |             + `movies`
16386 |             + `episodes`
16387 | 
16388 |     + start_at (optional, string, `2016-06-01T00:00:00.000Z`) ... Starting date.
16389 |     + end_at (optional, string, `2016-07-01T23:59:59.000Z`) ... Ending date.
16390 | 
16391 | ### Get playback progress [GET]
16392 | #### &#128274; OAuth Required &#128196; Pagination Optional
16393 | Whenever a scrobble is paused, the playback progress is saved. Use this progress to sync up playback across different media centers or apps. For example, you can start watching a movie in a media center, stop it, then resume on your tablet from the same spot. Each item will have the `progress` percentage between 0 and 100.
16394 | 
16395 | You can optionally specify a `type` to only get `movies` or `episodes`.
16396 | 
16397 | By default, all results will be returned. Pagination is optional and can be used for something like an "on deck" feature, or if you only need a limited data set.
16398 | 
16399 | > ### 🅽🅾🆃🅴
16400 | > _We only save playback progress for the last 6 months._

16480 | ## Get Collection [/sync/collection/{type}]
16481 | + Parameters
16482 |     + type (required, string, `movies`) ...
16483 | 
16484 |         + Values
16485 |             + `movies`
16486 |             + `shows`
16487 | 
16488 | ### Get collection [GET]
16489 | #### &#128274; OAuth Required &#10024; Extended Info
16490 | Get all collected items in a user's collection. A collected item indicates availability to watch digitally or on physical media.
16491 | 
16492 | Each `movie` object contains `collected_at` and `updated_at` timestamps. Since users can set custom dates when they collected movies, it is possible for `collected_at` to be in the past. We also include `updated_at` to help sync Trakt data with your app. Cache this timestamp locally and only re-process the movie if you see a newer timestamp.
16493 | 
16494 | Each `show` object contains `last_collected_at` and `last_updated_at` timestamps. Since users can set custom dates when they collected episodes, it is possible for `last_collected_at` to be in the past. We also include `last_updated_at` to help sync Trakt data with your app. Cache this timestamp locally and only re-process the show if you see a newer timestamp.
16495 | 
16496 | If you add `?extended=metadata` to the URL, it will return the additional `media_type`, `resolution`, `hdr`, `audio`, `audio_channels` and '3d' metadata. It will use `null` if the metadata isn't set for an item.
16497 |

16502 |             Authorization: Bearer [access_token]
16503 |             trakt-api-version: 2
16504 |             trakt-api-key: [client_id]
16505 |

16507 |

16510 |     ```

16858 | ## Add to Collection [/sync/collection]
16859 | 
16860 | ### Add items to collection [POST]
16861 | #### 🔥 VIP Enhanced &#128274; &#128274; OAuth Required
16862 | Add items to a user's collection. Accepts shows, seasons, episodes and movies. If only a show is passed, all episodes for the show will be collected. If seasons are specified, all episodes in those seasons will be collected.
16863 | 
16864 | Send a `collected_at` UTC datetime to mark items as collected in the past. You can also send additional metadata about the media itself to have a very accurate collection. Showcase what is available to watch from your epic HD DVD collection down to your downloaded iTunes movies.
16865 | 
16866 | #### Limits
16867 | 
16868 | If the user's collection limit is exceeded, a `420` HTTP error code is returned. Use the [**/users/settings**](/reference/users/settings) method to get all limits for a user account. In most cases, upgrading to [**Trakt VIP**](https://trakt.tv/vip) will increase the limits.
16869 | 
16870 | > ### 🅽🅾🆃🅴
16871 | > _You can resend items already in your collection and they will be updated with any new values. This includes the `collected_at` and any other metadata._
16872 | 
16873 | #### JSON POST Data
16874 | | Key | Type | Value |
16875 | |---|---|---|
16876 | | `movies` | array | Array of `movie` objects. (see examples &#8594;) |
16877 | | `shows` | array | Array of `show` objects. |
16878 | | `seasons` | array | Array of `season` objects. |
16879 | | `episodes` | array | Array of `episode` objects. |
16880 | 
16881 | #### Media Object POST Data
16882 | | Key | Type | Value |
16883 | |---|---|---|
16884 | | item <span style="color:red;">*</a> | object | `movie`, `show`, or `episode` object. |
16885 | | `collected_at` | datetime | UTC datetime when the item was collected. Set to `released` to automatically use the inital release date + runtime *(episodes only)*). |
16886 | | `media_type` | string | Set to `digital`, `bluray`, `hddvd`, `dvd`, `vcd`, `vhs`, `betamax`, or `laserdisc`. |
16887 | | `resolution` | string | Set to `uhd_4k`, `hd_1080p`, `hd_1080i`, `hd_720p`, `sd_480p`, `sd_480i`, `sd_576p`, or `sd_576i`. |
16888 | | `hdr` | string | Set to `dolby_vision`, `hdr10`, `hdr10_plus`, or `hlg`. |
16889 | | `audio` | string | Set to `dolby_digital`, `dolby_digital_plus`, `dolby_digital_plus_atmos`, `dolby_truehd`, `dolby_atmos` *(Dolby TrueHD Atmos)*, `dolby_prologic`, `dts`, `dts_ma`, `dts_hr`, `dts_x`, `auro_3d`, `mp3`, `mp2`, `aac`, `lpcm`, `ogg` *(Ogg Vorbis)*, `ogg_opus`, `wma`, or `flac`. |
16890 | | `audio_channels` | string | Set to `1.0`, `2.0`, `2.1`, `3.0`, `3.1`, `4.0`, `4.1`, `5.0`, `5.1`, `5.1.2`, `5.1.4`, `6.1`, `7.1`, `7.1.2`, `7.1.4`, `9.1`, or `10.1` |
16891 | | `3d` | boolean | Set `true` if in 3D. |
16892 | 
16893 | + Request (application/json)
16894 | 
16895 |     + Headers
16896 | 
16897 |             Authorization: Bearer [access_token]
16898 |             trakt-api-version: 2
16899 |             trakt-api-key: [client_id]
16900 | 
16901 |     + Body
