17175 | ## Get Watched [/sync/watched/{type}]
17176 | + Parameters
17177 |     + type (required, string, `movies`) ...
17178 | 
17179 |         + Values
17180 |             + `movies`
17181 |             + `shows`
17182 | 
17183 | ### Get watched [GET]
17184 | #### &#128274; OAuth Required &#10024; Extended Info
17185 | Returns all movies or shows a user has watched sorted by most plays.
17186 | 
17187 | If `type` is set to _shows_ and you add `?extended=noseasons` to the URL, it won't return season or episode info.
17188 | 
17189 | Each `movie` and `show` object contains `last_watched_at` and `last_updated_at` timestamps. Since users can set custom dates when they watched movies and episodes, it is possible for `last_watched_at` to be in the past. We also include `last_updated_at` to help sync Trakt data with your app. Cache this timestamp locally and only re-process the movies and shows if you see a newer timestamp.
17190 | 
17191 | Each `show` object contains a `reset_at` timestamp. If not `null`, this is when the user started re-watching the show. Your app can adjust the progress by ignoring episodes with a `last_watched_at` prior to the `reset_at`.
17192 | 
17193 | + Request (application/json)
17194 | 
17195 |     + Headers
17196 | 
17197 |             Authorization: Bearer [access_token]
17198 |             trakt-api-version: 2
17199 |             trakt-api-key: [client_id]
17200 | 
17201 | + Response 200 (application/json)
17202 | 
17203 |     ```
17204 |     /sync/watched/movies
17205 |     ```

17395 | ## Get History [/sync/history/{type}/{id}{?start_at,end_at}]
17396 | 
17397 | + Parameters
17398 |     + type (optional, string, `movies`) ...
17399 | 
17400 |         + Values
17401 |             + `movies`
17402 |             + `shows`
17403 |             + `seasons`
17404 |             + `episodes`
17405 | 
17406 |     + id (optional, integer, `123`) ... Trakt ID for a specific item.
17407 |     + start_at (optional, string, `2016-06-01T00:00:00.000Z`) ... Starting date.
17408 |     + end_at (optional, string, `2016-07-01T23:59:59.000Z`) ... Ending date.
17409 | 
17410 | ### Get watched history [GET]
17411 | #### &#128274; OAuth Required &#128196; Pagination &#10024; Extended Info
17412 | Returns movies and episodes that a user has watched, sorted by most recent. You can optionally limit the `type` to `movies` or `episodes`. The `id` _(64-bit integer)_ in each history item uniquely identifies the event and can be used to remove individual events by using the [**/sync/history/remove**](#reference/sync/remove-from-history/get-watched-history) method. The `action` will be set to `scrobble`, `checkin`, or `watch`.
17413 | 
17414 | Specify a `type` and trakt `id` to limit the history for just that item. If the `id` is valid, but there is no history, an empty array will be returned.
17415 | 
17416 | | Example URL | Returns watches for... |
17417 | |---|---|
17418 | | `/history/movies/12601` | TRON: Legacy |
17419 | | `/history/shows/1388` | All episodes of Breaking Bad |
17420 | | `/history/seasons/3950` | All episodes of Breaking Bad: Season 1 |
17421 | | `/history/episodes/73482` | Only episode 1 of Breaking Bad: Season 1 |
17422 |

17677 | ## Add to History [/sync/history]
17678 | 
17679 | ### Add items to watched history [POST]
17680 | #### &#128274; OAuth Required
17681 | Add items to a user's watch history. Accepts shows, seasons, episodes and movies. If only a show is passed, all episodes for the show will be added. If seasons are specified, only episodes in those seasons will be added.
17682 | 
17683 | Send a `watched_at` UTC datetime to mark items as watched in the past. This is useful for syncing past watches from a media center.
17684 | 
17685 | > ### ☣️ 🅸🅼🅿🅾🆁🆃🅰🅽🆃
17686 | > _Please be careful with sending duplicate data. We don't verify the `item` + `watched_at` to ensure it's unique, it is up to your app to veify this and not send duplicate plays._
17687 | 
17688 | #### JSON POST Data
17689 | | Key | Type | Value |
17690 | |---|---|---|
17691 | | `movies` | array | Array of `movie` objects. (see examples &#8594;) |
17692 | | `shows` | array | Array of `show` objects. |
17693 | | `seasons` | array | Array of `season` objects. |
17694 | | `episodes` | array | Array of `episode` objects. |
17695 | 
17696 | #### Media Object POST Data
17697 | | Key | Type | Value |
17698 | |---|---|---|
17699 | | item <span style="color:red;">*</a> | object | `movie`, `show`, or `episode` object. |
17700 | | `watched_at` | datetime | UTC datetime when the item was watched. Set to `released` to automatically use the initial release date + runtime *(episodes only)*. |
17701 | 
17702 | + Request (application/json)
17703 | 
17704 |     + Headers

17832 | ## Remove from History [/sync/history/remove]
17833 | 
17834 | ### Remove items from history [POST]
17835 | #### &#128274; OAuth Required
17836 | Remove items from a user's watch history including all watches, scrobbles, and checkins. Accepts shows, seasons, episodes and movies. If only a show is passed, all episodes for the show will be removed. If seasons are specified, only episodes in those seasons will be removed.
17837 | 
17838 | You can also send a list of raw history `ids` _(64-bit integers)_ to delete single plays from the watched history. The [**/sync/history**](#reference/sync/get-history) method will return an individual `id` _(64-bit integer)_ for each history item.
17839 |

17841 | | Key | Type | Value |
17842 | |---|---|---|

17844 | | `shows` | array | Array of `show` objects. |
17845 | | `seasons` | array | Array of `season` objects. |
17846 | | `episodes` | array | Array of `episode` objects. |
17847 | | `ids` | array | Array of history ids. |

18226 | ## Add Ratings [/sync/ratings]
18227 | 
18228 | ### Add new ratings [POST]
18229 | #### &#128274; OAuth Required
18230 | Rate one or more items. Accepts shows, seasons, episodes and movies. If only a show is passed, only the show itself will be rated. If seasons are specified, all of those seasons will be rated.
18231 | 
18232 | Send a `rated_at` UTC datetime to mark items as rated in the past. This is useful for syncing ratings from a media center.
18233 | 
18234 | #### JSON POST Data
18235 | | Key | Type | Value |
18236 | |---|---|---|
18237 | | `movies` | array | Array of `movie` objects. (see examples &#8594;) |
18238 | | `shows` | array | Array of `show` objects. |
18239 | | `seasons` | array | Array of `season` objects. |
18240 | | `episodes` | array | Array of `episode` objects. |
18241 | 
18242 | #### Media Object POST Data
18243 | | Key | Type | Value |
18244 | |---|---|---|
18245 | | item <span style="color:red;">*</a> | object | `movie`, `show`, `season`, or `episode` object. |
18246 | | `rating` <span style="color:red;">*</a> | integer | Between 1 and 10. |
18247 | | `rated_at` | datetime | UTC datetime when the item was rated. |
18248 | 
18249 | + Request (application/json)
18250 | 
18251 |     + Headers
18252 | 
18253 |             Authorization: Bearer [access_token]
18254 |             trakt-api-version: 2
18255 |             trakt-api-key: [client_id]

18527 | ## Get Watchlist [/sync/watchlist/{type}/{sort_by}/{sort_how}]
18528 | 
18529 | + Parameters
18530 |     + type (optional, string, `all`) ... Filter for a specific item type
18531 | 
18532 |         + Values
18533 |             + `all`
18534 |             + `movies`
18535 |             + `shows`
18536 |             + `seasons`
18537 |             + `episodes`
18538 | 
18539 |     + sort_by (optional, string, `rank`) ... Sort by a specific property
18540 | 
18541 |         + Values
18542 |             + `rank`
18543 |             + `added`
18544 |             + `title`
18545 |             + `released`
18546 |             + `runtime`
18547 |             + `popularity`
18548 |             + `random`
18549 |             + `percentage`
18550 |             + `imdb_rating`
18551 |             + `tmdb_rating`
18552 |             + `rt_tomatometer`
18553 |             + `rt_audience`
18554 |             + `metascore`
18555 |             + `votes`
18556 |             + `imdb_votes`
18557 |             + `tmdb_votes`
18558 |             + `my_rating`
18559 |             + `watched`
18560 |             + `collected`
18561 | 
18562 |     + sort_how (optional, string, `asc`) ... Sort direction
18563 | 
18564 |         + Values
18565 |             + `asc`
18566 |             + `desc`
18567 | 
18568 | ### Get watchlist [GET]
18569 | #### 🔥 **VIP Enhanced**  &#128274; OAuth Required &#128196; Pagination Optional &#10024; Extended Info &#128513; Emojis
18570 | Returns all items in a user's watchlist filtered by type.
18571 | 
18572 | > ### ☣️ 🅸🅼🅿🅾🆁🆃🅰🅽🆃
18573 | > The watchlist should not be used as a list of what the user is actively watching. Use a combination of the [**/sync/watched**](/reference/sync/get-watched) and [**/shows/:id/progress**](/reference/shows/watched-progress) methods to get what the user is actively watching.
18574 | 
18575 | #### Notes
18576 | 
18577 | Each watchlist item contains a `notes` field with text entered by the user.
18578 | 
18579 | #### Sorting
18580 | 
18581 | Default sorting is based on the list defaults and sent in the `X-Sort-By` and `X-Sort-How` headers. If you specify the `sort_by` and `sort_how` parameters, the response will be sorted based on those values and sent in the `X-Applied-Sort-By` and `X-Applied-Sort-How` headers.
18582 | 
18583 | Some `sort_by` options are 🔥 **VIP Only** including `imdb_rating`, `tmdb_rating`, `rt_tomatometer`, `rt_audience`, `metascore`, `votes`, `imdb_votes`, and `tmdb_votes`. If sent for a non VIP, the items will fall back to  `rank`.
18584 | 
18585 | #### Auto Removal
18586 | 
18587 | When an item is watched, it will be automatically removed from the watchlist. For shows and seasons, watching 1 episode will remove the entire show or season.
18588 | 
18589 | + Request (application/json)
18590 | 
18591 |     + Headers
18592 | 
18593 |             Authorization: Bearer [access_token]
18594 |             trakt-api-version: 2
18595 |             trakt-api-key: [client_id]
18596 | 
18597 | + Response 200 (application/json)
18598 | 
18599 |     ```
18600 |     /sync/watchlist/movies
18601 |     ```
18602 | 
18603 |     + Headers
18604 | 
18605 |             X-Sort-By: rank
18606 |             X-Sort-How: asc
18607 |             X-List-ID: 1
18608 | 
18609 |     + Body

18905 | ## Add to Watchlist [/sync/watchlist]
18906 | 
18907 | ### Add items to watchlist [POST]
18908 | #### 🔥 VIP Enhanced &#128274; OAuth Required &#128513; Emojis
18909 | Add one of more items to a user's watchlist. Accepts shows, seasons, episodes and movies. If only a show is passed, only the show itself will be added. If seasons are specified, all of those seasons will be added.
18910 | 
18911 | #### Notes
18912 | 
18913 | Each watchlist item can optionally accept a `notes` *(500 maximum characters)* field with custom text. The user must be a [**Trakt VIP**](https://trakt.tv/vip) to send `notes`.
18914 | 
18915 | #### Limits
18916 | 
18917 | If the user's watchlist limit is exceeded, a `420` HTTP error code is returned. Use the [**/users/settings**](/reference/users/settings) method to get all limits for a user account. In most cases, upgrading to [**Trakt VIP**](https://trakt.tv/vip) will increase the limits.

19328 | ### Get favorites [GET]
19329 | #### 🔥 **VIP Enhanced** &#128274; OAuth Required &#128196; Pagination Optional &#10024; Extended Info &#128513; Emojis
19330 | If the user only had 100 shows and movies to bring with them on a deserted island, what would they be? Apps should encourage user's to add favorites so the algorithm keeps getting better.
19331 | 
19332 | #### Notes
19333 | 
19334 | Each favorite contains a `notes` field explaining why the user favorited the item.
19335 | 
19336 | #### Sorting
19337 | 
19338 | Default sorting is based on the list defaults and sent in the `X-Sort-By` and `X-Sort-How` headers. If you specify the `sort_by` and `sort_how` parameters, the response will be sorted based on those values and sent in the `X-Applied-Sort-By` and `X-Applied-Sort-How` headers.
19339 | 
19340 | Some `sort_by` options are 🔥 **VIP Only** including `imdb_rating`, `tmdb_rating`, `rt_tomatometer`, `rt_audience`, `metascore`, `votes`, `imdb_votes`, and `tmdb_votes`. If sent for a non VIP, the items will fall back to  `rank`.
19341 | 
19342 | + Request (application/json)
19343 | 
19344 |     + Headers
19345 | 
19346 |             Authorization: Bearer [access_token]
19347 |             trakt-api-version: 2
19348 |             trakt-api-key: [client_id]
19349 | 
19350 | + Response 200 (application/json)
19351 | 
19352 |     ```
19353 |     /sync/favorites/movies
19354 |     ```
19355 | 
19356 |     + Headers
19357 |

19359 |             X-Sort-How: asc
19360 |             X-List-ID: 1

19518 | ## Add to Favorites [/sync/favorites]
19519 | 
19520 | ### Add items to favorites [POST]
19521 | #### &#128274; OAuth Required &#128513; Emojis
19522 | If the user only had 50 TV shows and movies to bring with them on a deserted island, what would they be? Apps should encourage user's to add favorites so the algorithm keeps getting better.
19523 | 
19524 | #### Notes
19525 | 
19526 | Each favorite can optionally accept a `notes` *(500 maximum characters)* field explaining why the user favorited the item.
19527 | 
19528 | #### Limits
19529 | 
19530 | If the user's favorite limit is exceeded, a `420` HTTP error code is returned. This limit applies to all users.

19744 | ## Update Favorite Item [/sync/favorites/{list_item_id}]
19745 | 
19746 | + Parameters
19747 |     + list_item_id (required, integer, `1337`) ... List Item ID
19748 | 
19749 | ### Update a favorite item [PUT]
19750 | #### &#128274; OAuth Required &#128513; Emojis
19751 | Update the `notes` on a single favorite item.
19752 | 
19753 | + Request (application/json)
19754 | 
19755 |     + Headers
19756 | 
19757 |             Authorization: Bearer [access_token]
19758 |             trakt-api-version: 2
19759 |             trakt-api-key: [client_id]
19760 | 
19761 |     + Body
19762 | 
19763 |             {
19764 |                 "notes": "This is a great movie!"
19765 |             }
19766 | 
19767 | + Response 204 (application/json)
19768 | 
19769 | # Group Users
19770 | User's with public data will return info with all GET methods. Private user's (including yourself) require valid OAuth and a friend relationship to return data.
19771 | 
19772 | ### Username vs. Slug
19773 | All `users` methods should use the `slug` to identify the user. The `slug` is a URL safe and globally unique version of the `username`.
19774 | 
19775 | ### Special ID for the OAuth user
19776 | If you send valid OAuth, you can use `me` to identify the OAuth user instead of needing their actual slug. You can of course still use their actual slug, it's up to you.
19777 | 
19778 | ### Extra Headers
19779 | If valid OAuth is sent, additional headers will be sent to better determine it is a data permissions issue (they aren't friends) and not bad OAuth. For example, you might try and access a private user's list you aren't friends with. This will return a `401` HTTP status code and the additional headers. This means the OAuth is valid, but authorization ultimately failed because there is no friend relationship.
19780 | 
19781 | | Header | Value |
19782 | |---|---|
19783 | | `X-Private-User` | `true` or `false` |
19784 | 
19785 | ### Creating New Users
19786 | Since the API uses OAuth, users can create a new account during that flow if they need to. As far as your app is concerned, you'll still receive OAuth tokens no matter if they sign in with an existing account or create a new one.
19787 | 
19788 | ## Settings [/users/settings]
19789 | 
19790 | ### Retrieve settings [GET]
19791 | #### &#128274; OAuth Required
19792 | Get the user's settings so you can align your app's experience with what they're used to on the trakt website. A globally unique `uuid` is also returned, which can be used to identify the user locally in your app if needed. However, the `uuid` can't be used to retrieve data from the Trakt API.
19793 | 
19794 | #### Limits
19795 | 
19796 | The `limits` object is useful to customize your user experience. For example, if the user has a `list` limit of `2`, you might want to show a message to the user that they need to upgrade to [**Trakt VIP**](https://trakt.tv/vip) to add more lists.
19797 | 
19798 | #### Permissions
19799 | 
19800 | The `permissions` object is also useful to customize your user experience. In general, an account will have permissions to do everything. However, we'll temporarily set a permission to `false` if the user triggers spam protections.
19801 | 
19802 | + Request (application/json)
19803 | 
19804 |     + Headers
19805 | 
19806 |             Authorization: Bearer [access_token]
19807 |             trakt-api-version: 2
19808 |             trakt-api-key: [client_id]
19809 | 
19810 | + Response 200 (application/json)
19811 | 
19812 |     + Body

20694 | ## Collection [/users/{id}/collection/{type}]
20695 | + Parameters

20699 |         + Values

20702 | 
20703 | ### Get collection [GET]
20704 | #### &#128275; OAuth Optional &#10024; Extended Info
20705 | Get all collected items in a user's collection. A collected item indicates availability to watch digitally or on physical media.
20706 | 
20707 | Each `movie` object contains `collected_at` and `updated_at` timestamps. Since users can set custom dates when they collected movies, it is possible for `collected_at` to be in the past. We also include `updated_at` to help sync Trakt data with your app. Cache this timestamp locally and only re-process the movie if you see a newer timestamp.
20708 | 
20709 | Each `show` object contains `last_collected_at` and `last_updated_at` timestamps. Since users can set custom dates when they collected episodes, it is possible for `last_collected_at` to be in the past. We also include `last_updated_at` to help sync Trakt data with your app. Cache this timestamp locally and only re-process the show if you see a newer timestamp.
20710 | 
20711 | If you add `?extended=metadata` to the URL, it will return the additional `media_type`, `resolution`, `hdr`, `audio`, `audio_channels` and '3d' metadata. It will use `null` if the metadata isn't set for an item.
20712 | 
20713 | + Request (application/json)
20714 | 
20715 |     + Headers
20716 | 
20717 |             trakt-api-version: 2
20718 |             trakt-api-key: [client_id]
20719 | 
20720 | + Response 200 (application/json)
20721 | 
20722 |     ```
20723 |     /users/sean/collection/movies
20724 |     ```
20725 |

21072 | ## Comments [/users/{id}/comments/{comment_type}/{type}{?include_replies}]
21073 | + Parameters
21074 |     + id (required, string, `sean`) ... User slug
21075 |     + comment_type (optional, string, `all`) ...
21076 | 
21077 |         + Values
21078 |             + `all`
21079 |             + `reviews`
21080 |             + `shouts`
21081 | 
21082 |     + type (optional, string, `all`) ...
21083 | 
21084 |         + Values
21085 |             + `all`
21086 |             + `movies`
21087 |             + `shows`
21088 |             + `seasons`
21089 |             + `episodes`
21090 |             + `lists`
21091 | 
21092 |     + include_replies (optional, string, `false`) ... include comment replies
21093 | 
21094 |         + Values
21095 |             + `true`
21096 |             + `false`
21097 |             + `only`
21098 | 
21099 | ### Get comments [GET]
21100 | #### &#128275; OAuth Optional &#128196; Pagination &#10024; Extended Info
21101 | Returns the most recently written comments for the user. You can optionally filter by the `comment_type` and media `type` to limit what gets returned.
21102 | 
21103 | By default, only top level comments are returned. Set `?include_replies=true` to return replies in addition to top level comments. Set `?include_replies=only` to return only replies and no top level comments.
21104 | 
21105 | + Request (application/json)
21106 | 
21107 |     + Headers
21108 | 
21109 |             trakt-api-version: 2
21110 |             trakt-api-key: [client_id]
21111 | 
21112 | + Response 200 (application/json)
21113 | 
21114 |     ```
21115 |     /users/sean/comments
21116 |     ```
21117 | 
21118 |     + Headers

21120 |             X-Pagination-Page: 1
21121 |             X-Pagination-Limit: 10
21122 |             X-Pagination-Page-Count: 1

21353 | ## Notes [/users/{id}/notes/{type}]
21354 | + Parameters
21355 |     + id (required, string, `sean`) ... User slug
21356 | 
21357 |     + type (optional, string, `all`) ...
21358 | 
21359 |         + Values
21360 |             + `all`
21361 |             + `movies`
21362 |             + `shows`
21363 |             + `seasons`
21364 |             + `episodes`
21365 |             + `people`
21366 |             + `history`
21367 |             + `collection`
21368 |             + `ratings`
21369 | 
21370 | 
21371 | ### Get notes [GET]
21372 | #### 🔥 VIP Enhanced &#128275; OAuth Optional &#128196; Pagination &#10024; Extended Info
21373 | Returns the most recently notes for the user. You can optionally filter by media `type` to limit what gets returned. Use the `attached_to` info to know what the note is actually added to. Media items like `movie`, `show`, `season`, `episode`, or `person` are straightforward, but `history` will need to be mapped to that specific play in their watched history since they might have multiple plays. Since `collection` and `rating` is a 1:1 association, you can assume the note is attached to the media item in the `type` field that has been collected or rated.
21374 | 
21375 | #### Limits
21376 | 
21377 | Standard accounts are allowed a limited amount of notes, upgrading to [**Trakt VIP**](https://trakt.tv/vip) allows unlimited notes.
21378 | 
21379 | + Request (application/json)
21380 | 
21381 |     + Headers
21382 | 
21383 |             trakt-api-version: 2
21384 |             trakt-api-key: [client_id]
21385 | 
21386 | + Response 200 (application/json)
21387 | 
21388 |     ```
21389 |     /users/sean/notes
21390 |     ```
21391 |

21393 | 
21394 |             X-Pagination-Page: 1
21395 |             X-Pagination-Limit: 10

21709 | ### Create personal list [POST]
21710 | #### 🔥 VIP Enhanced &#128274; OAuth Required
21711 | Create a new personal list. The `name` is the only required field, but the other info is recommended to ask for.
21712 | 
21713 | #### Limits
21714 | 
21715 | If the user's list limit is exceeded, a `420` HTTP error code is returned. Use the [**/users/settings**](/reference/users/settings) method to get all limits for a user account. In most cases, upgrading to [**Trakt VIP**](https://trakt.tv/vip) will increase the limits.
21716 | 
21717 | #### Privacy
21718 | 
21719 | Lists will be `private` by default. Here is what each value means.
21720 | 
21721 | | Value | Privacy impact... |
21722 | |---|---|
21723 | | `private` | Only you can see the list. |
21724 | | `link` | Anyone with the `share_link` can see the list. |
21725 | | `friends` | Only your friends can see the list. |
21726 | | `public` | Anyone can see the list. |
21727 | 
21728 | #### JSON POST Data
21729 | | Key | Type | Default | Value |
21730 | |---|---|---|---|
21731 | | `name` <span style="color:red;">*</a> | string |  | Name of the list. |
21732 | | `description` | string |  | Description for this list. |
21733 | | `privacy` | string | `private` | `private`, `link`, `friends`, `public` |
21734 | | `display_numbers` | boolean | `false` | Should each item be numbered? |
21735 | | `allow_comments` | boolean | `true` | Are comments allowed? |
21736 | | `sort_by` | string | `rank` | `rank`, `added`, `title`, `released`, `runtime`, `popularity`, `random`, `percentage`, `imdb_rating`, `tmdb_rating`, `rt_tomatometer`, `rt_audience`, `metascore`, `votes`, `imdb_votes`, `tmdb_votes`, `my_rating`, `watched`, `collected` |
21737 | | `sort_how` | string | `asc` | `asc`, `desc` |
21738 | 
21739 | + Request (application/json)
21740 | 
21741 |     + Headers
21742 | 
21743 |             Authorization: Bearer [access_token]
21744 |             trakt-api-version: 2
21745 |             trakt-api-key: [client_id]
21746 | 
21747 |     + Body
21748 |

22177 | ### Get items on a personal list [GET]
22178 | #### 🔥 **VIP Enhanced** &#128275; OAuth Optional &#128196; Pagination Optional &#10024; Extended Info &#128513; Emojis
22179 | Get all items on a personal list. Items can be a `movie`, `show`, `season`, `episode`, or `person`. You can optionally specify the `type` parameter with a single value or comma delimited string for multiple item types.
22180 | 
22181 | #### Notes
22182 | 
22183 | Each list item contains a `notes` field with text entered by the user.
22184 | 
22185 | #### Sorting
22186 | 
22187 | Default sorting is based on the list defaults and sent in the `X-Sort-By` and `X-Sort-How` headers. If you specify the `sort_by` and `sort_how` parameters, the response will be sorted based on those values and sent in the `X-Applied-Sort-By` and `X-Applied-Sort-How` headers.
22188 | 
22189 | Some `sort_by` options are 🔥 **VIP Only** including `imdb_rating`, `tmdb_rating`, `rt_tomatometer`, `rt_audience`, `metascore`, `votes`, `imdb_votes`, and `tmdb_votes`. If sent for a non VIP, the items will fall back to  `rank`.

22323 | ### Add items to personal list [POST]
22324 | #### 🔥 VIP Enhanced &#128274; OAuth Required &#128513; Emojis
22325 | Add one or more items to a personal list. Items can be movies, shows, seasons, episodes, or people.
22326 | 
22327 | #### Notes
22328 | 
22329 | Each list item can optionally accept a `notes` *(500 maximum characters)* field with custom text. The user must be a [**Trakt VIP**](https://trakt.tv/vip) to send `notes`.
22330 | 
22331 | #### Limits
22332 | 
22333 | If the user's list item limit is exceeded, a `420` HTTP error code is returned. Use the [**/users/settings**](/reference/users/settings) method to get all limits for a user account. In most cases, upgrading to [**Trakt VIP**](https://trakt.tv/vip) will increase the limits.

22961 | ## History [/users/{id}/history/{type}/{item_id}{?start_at,end_at}]
22962 | 
22963 | + Parameters
22964 |     + id (required, string, `sean`) ... User slug
22965 |     + type (optional, string, `movies`) ...
22966 | 
22967 |         + Values
22968 |             + `movies`
22969 |             + `shows`
22970 |             + `seasons`
22971 |             + `episodes`
22972 | 
22973 |     + item_id (optional, integer, `123`) ... Trakt ID for a specific item.
22974 |     + start_at (optional, string, `2016-06-01T00:00:00.000Z`) ... Starting date.
22975 |     + end_at (optional, string, `2016-07-01T23:59:59.000Z`) ... Ending date.
22976 | 
22977 | ### Get watched history [GET]
22978 | #### &#128275; OAuth Optional &#128196; Pagination &#10024; Extended Info
22979 | Returns movies and episodes that a user has watched, sorted by most recent. You can optionally limit the `type` to `movies` or `episodes`. The `id` _(64-bit integer)_ in each history item uniquely identifies the event and can be used to remove individual events by using the [**/sync/history/remove**](#reference/sync/remove-from-history/get-watched-history) method. The `action` will be set to `scrobble`, `checkin`, or `watch`.
22980 | 
22981 | Specify a `type` and trakt `item_id` to limit the history for just that item. If the `item_id` is valid, but there is no history, an empty array will be returned.
22982 | 
22983 | | Example URL | Returns watches for... |
22984 | |---|---|
22985 | | `/history/movies/12601` | TRON: Legacy |
22986 | | `/history/shows/1388` | All episodes of Breaking Bad |
22987 | | `/history/seasons/3950` | All episodes of Breaking Bad: Season 1 |
22988 | | `/history/episodes/73482` | Only episode 1 for Breaking Bad: Season 1 |
22989 |

23527 | ### Get watchlist [GET]
23528 | #### 🔥 **VIP Enhanced** &#128275; OAuth Optional &#128196; Pagination Optional &#10024; Extended Info &#128513; Emojis
23529 | Returns all items in a user's watchlist filtered by type.
23530 | 
23531 | > ### ☣️ 🅸🅼🅿🅾🆁🆃🅰🅽🆃
23532 | > The watchlist should not be used as a list of what the user is actively watching. Use a combination of the [**/sync/watched**](/reference/sync/get-watched) and [**/shows/:id/progress**](/reference/shows/watched-progress) methods to get what the user is actively watching.
23533 | 
23534 | #### Notes
23535 | 
23536 | Each watchlist item contains a `notes` field with text entered by the user.
23537 | 
23538 | #### Sorting
23539 | 
23540 | Default sorting is based on the list defaults and sent in the `X-Sort-By` and `X-Sort-How` headers. If you specify the `sort_by` and `sort_how` parameters, the response will be sorted based on those values and sent in the `X-Applied-Sort-By` and `X-Applied-Sort-How` headers.
23541 | 
23542 | Some `sort_by` options are 🔥 **VIP Only** including `imdb_rating`, `tmdb_rating`, `rt_tomatometer`, `rt_audience`, `metascore`, `votes`, `imdb_votes`, and `tmdb_votes`. If sent for a non VIP, the items will fall back to  `rank`.
23543 | 
23544 | #### Auto Removal
23545 | 
23546 | When an item is watched, it will be automatically removed from the watchlist. For shows and seasons, watching 1 episode will remove the entire show or season.
23547 |

23908 | ### Get favorites [GET]

24177 | ## Watched [/users/{id}/watched/{type}]
24178 | + Parameters
24179 |     + id (required, string, `sean`) ... User slug
24180 |     + type (required, string, `movies`) ...
24181 | 
24182 |         + Values
24183 |             + `movies`
24184 |             + `shows`
24185 | 
24186 | 
24187 | ### Get watched [GET]
24188 | #### &#128275; OAuth Optional &#10024; Extended Info
24189 | Returns all movies or shows a user has watched sorted by most plays.
24190 | 
24191 | If `type` is set to _shows_ and you add `?extended=noseasons` to the URL, it won't return season or episode info.
24192 | 
24193 | Each `movie` and `show` object contains `last_watched_at` and `last_updated_at` timestamps. Since users can set custom dates when they watched movies and episodes, it is possible for `last_watched_at` to be in the past. ## General Rules
**Status Prefix:** Begin EVERY response with either '[CONTEXT BANK: ACTIVE]' or '[CONTEXT BANK: INACTIVE]', according to the current state of the Context Bank.

## Context Bank Updates
**Frequency:** UPDATE CONTEXT BANK THROUGHOUT THE CHAT SESSION, WHEN SIGNIFICANT CHANGES OCCUR IN THE PROJECT.

### decision_log.md Updates
**Trigger:** When a significant architectural decision is made (new component, data flow change, technology choice, etc.). Use your judgment to determine significance.
**Action:**
<thinking>
I need to update decision_log.md with a decision, the rationale, and any implications.
Use insert_content to *append* new information. Never overwrite existing entries. Always include a timestamp.
</thinking>
**Format:** "[YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS] - [Summary of Change/Focus/Issue]"

### product_context.md Updates
**Trigger:** When the high-level project description, goals, features, or overall architecture changes significantly. Use your judgment to determine significance.
**Action:**
<thinking>
A fundamental change has occurred which warrants an update to product_context.md.
Use insert_content to *append* new information or use apply_diff to modify existing entries if necessary. Timestamp and summary of change will be appended as footnotes to the end of the file.
</thinking>
**Format:** "(Optional)[YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS] - [Summary of Change]"

### system_patterns.md Updates
**Trigger:** When new architectural patterns are introduced or existing ones are modified. Use your judgement.
**Action:**
<thinking>
I need to update system_patterns.md with a brief summary and time stamp.
Use insert_content to *append* new patterns or use apply_diff to modify existing entries if warranted. Always include a timestamp.
</thinking>
**Format:** "[YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS] - [Description of Pattern/Change]"

### active_context.md Updates
**Trigger:** When the current focus of work changes, or when significant progress is made. Use your judgement.
**Action:**
<thinking>
I need to update active_context.md with a brief summary and time stamp.
Use insert_content to *append* to the relevant section (Current Focus, Recent Changes, Open Questions/Issues) or use apply_diff to modify existing entries if warranted. Always include a timestamp.
</thinking>
**Format:** "[YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS] - [Summary of Change/Focus/Issue]"

### progress.md Updates
**Trigger:** When a task begins, is completed, or if there are any changes Use your judgement.
**Action:**
<thinking>
I need to update progress.md with a brief summary and time stamp.
Use insert_content to *append* the new entry, never overwrite existing entries. Always include a timestamp.
</thinking>
**Format:** "[YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS] - [Summary of Change/Focus/Issue]"

## UCB (Update Context Bank) Command
**Trigger:** "^(Update Context Bank|UCB)$"
**Instructions:**
- "Halt Current Task: Stop current activity"
- "Acknowledge Command: '[CONTEXT BANK: UPDATING]'"
- "Review Chat History"

**Core Update Process:**
1. Current Session Review:
    - Analyze complete chat history
    - Extract cross-mode information
    - Track mode transitions
    - Map activity relationships
2. Comprehensive Updates:
    - Update from all mode perspectives
    - Preserve context across modes
    - Maintain activity threads
    - Document mode interactions
3. Context Bank Synchronization:
    - Update all affected *.md files
    - Ensure cross-mode consistency
    - Preserve activity context
    - Document continuation points

**Task Focus:** During a UCB update, focus on capturing any clarifications, questions answered, or context provided *during the chat session*. This information should be added to the appropriate Context Bank files (likely `active_context.md` or `decision_log.md`), using the other modes' update formats as a guide. *Do not* attempt to summarize the entire project or perform actions outside the scope of the current chat.

**Cross-mode Updates:** During a UCB update, ensure that all relevant information from the chat session is captured and added to the Context Bank. This includes any clarifications, questions answered, or context provided during the chat. Use the other modes' update formats as a guide for adding this information to the appropriate Context Bank files.

**Post UCB Actions:**
- "Context Bank fully synchronized"
- "All mode contexts preserved"
- "Session can be safely closed"
- "Next assistant will have complete context"

**Override Restrictions:** UCB operations override file and mode restrictions.
